description.en: A shared discovery group for the early chapters of human history. Regional period definitions and dates differ; chapters can overlap in time. Each chapter shows its own time span.

sourceRefs.locator: 29 November 2021, “Antecedentes históricos” and “Antes de la segunda guerra mundial”: September 1882 opening, choice of the slope of Cerro Ancón to catch breezes away from city wastewater, US acquisition and reuse of the grounds. MINSA gives 12 September for the opening. The thanksgiving Mass is separately dated to the 17th by Escobar. The station therefore identifies the opening by month.

Chapter VI, “Hospitales en la Época del Canal Francés”, pp. CXLIX–CLI. Companyo, his earlier work at Suez, Huerta de Gallo, the fundraising committee, the September thanksgiving Mass, transfers of patients, the sisters, Colón, the former Taboga hotel and the orphanage. Chapter VII, pp. CLXXIV–CLXXVI, reports the 1916 request for larger premises and lottery funding. Pp. CLXXXII–CLXXXIII name the four nursing graduates of 1912. For the 1924 opening date use the contemporary decrees, which supersede the December date printed on p. CLXXV.

“Gustave Eiffel”, final paragraphs on the first canal company, receivership and the appointment of a liquidator. Escobar, pp. CL–CLI, traces how the breakdown of the construction enterprise affected its hospitals.

Public Health Reports 19 (8), 19 February 1904, printed p. 277, “Hospitals”: wooden, separated pavilions of the French hospital, nursing by Sisters of Charity, twenty-four patients in the foreign section and twenty in the canal section. This is a count made before the US canal administration assumed the hospital.

Minutes, 118th meeting at Washington, 24 December 1906, printed p. 49, item 2. The Chief Sanitary Officer’s 1 December communication gives 7 June 1904 as the beginning of the service of “Miss M. Eugenie Hibbard” as chief nurse at Ancon Hospital. This is the credited start of her appointment.

The Panama Canal Review en Español, spring 1976, printed pp. 32–33. Hernández calls her Mary Eugene Hibbard, dates her appointment to June 1904, describes her arrival with Gorgas and two nurses, and quotes her recollections of some 75 scattered buildings and the five buildings selected for ward and service uses.

Doctoral thesis, printed p. 50, citing Rodríguez on the 1904 appointment and 1908 count of 117 nurses among 205 US women employed in the Canal Zone. Note 49 quotes La Estrella de Panamá, 9 February 1905, vol. LVI, no. 13544, p. 10, on malaria admissions and the latrines at Ancón. Pp. 52–53 quote the same newspaper of 13 March 1909 on admission of single women aged sixteen to twenty-five at Santo Tomás.

Service Records Cards, 1904–1920, series NAID 7226556. Illustration captioned “Miss Anna L. Doolittle, June 21, 1907 Service Card”, recto and verso, followed by Brown’s identification of her age, home in West Virginia and Ancon Hospital appointment. The full-size image linked farther down is separately identified as Ward 9, NAID 6120319.

Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 719, pp. 707–708. Enclosure is dated 20 January, cover letter 24 January, supplementary note 25 January. Eighteen official reports since 1 July 1904 included the four sanitary labourers still in hospital on 20 January. Three deaths, the cities and intervening zone, bills of health for shipping and the reported recoveries appear in the circular and note.

Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 718, pp. 706–707, especially enclosure 2, the translated reply of Panama’s minister of government and foreign affairs, 21 January 1905. De la Guardia explains his authorization and the changes suggested by his office when accepting the sanitary regulations under article VII.

Foreign Relations of the United States, 1905, document 723, enclosure 2, paragraph beginning “Immediately after seeing”. Barrett locates the legation near the corner of the canal building and the Plaza. The square serves only to orient the January circular in the capital. Its text gives no legation street address.

Societas 19 (1), 73–91, printed p. 78. Paragraph immediately preceding “El puerto de La Boca – Balboa”: engineers’ selection of the old French reservoir on the upper Río Grande and water running through Panama City’s mains on 4 July 1905.

Passages following the reorganization under David H. Brandon. The hydrant system was inaugurated in Cathedral Square on 4 July 1905. At the Malambo fire of 12 January 1906 the firefighters used pumps connected to cisterns.

Printed pp. 178–179, paragraph beginning “Uno de tales proyectos”: the Star and Herald / La Estrella called for water mains in the 1880s for drinking water and fire protection and reported on the municipal water contract in 1888.

Environmental History 21 (2), 250–259. Final paragraphs before “Panamanian Resistance” and paragraphs 1–4 of that section, notes 11–15. Describes rainwater, water peddlers, cisterns and ceramic tinajas, the reach of the dipper, topping up jars, complaints when inspectors emptied them and reports of residents concealing their jars.

National Archives Identifier 6120319, 185-G-16-1514, August 1919. National Archives Foundation, DocsTeach, “Citation” and item-specific “Rights: Public Domain”. The photographer is unnamed. The lower edge of the surviving print reads 284-X8, whereas the DocsTeach transcription renders 248-X8. Both identify the same image by title, month and NAID.

Image 88b710, source “The U.S. National Archives”, copyright field “No known copyright restrictions”. The photographic caption dates the picture to August 1919, without a day. The matched, full-size scan of NAID 6120319 used here is the one provided by the Archives on its Rediscovering Black History page.

The Panama Canal Record, vol. XIII, no. 1, 20 August 1919, printed p. 8 (PDF p. 26), table for the new hospital buildings. Section C, ward 9: 39 beds, official category “White foreign, male”. Wards 10–14 are separately classified. Compare visiting hours in sections A and C, and the note below the table assigning emergency passes to the section nurse.

Prologue 29 (2). Notes 1 and 2 identify Commissary manager to J. F. Stevens, 15 February 1907, and Stevens to W. C. Gorgas, 30 November 1906, both RG 185, General Correspondence 1904–14, file 2-C-55, part 1. Quotations, financial bonds, equivalent silver pay and access to facilities appear in the opening discussion of the two rolls.

Decree of 2 September 1924, Gaceta Oficial no. 4487, 13 September 1924, printed p. 393, left column, “Artículo único”, signed Porras and Jiménez. The text places in public service the hospital built by the nation on a Panama City site fronting Avenida Federico Boyd in the former Exposición Nacional area. PDF p. 2 is a facsimile.

Decree of 7 March 1924, arts. 1 and 3. The former exhibition grounds and the intended opening on 1 September are explicit. The programme is to include a reception and celebrations for administrative staff and convalescent patients. These are instructions for the celebration.

Memoria del Hospital Santo Tomás 2020–2021, “Recordar es vivir”, caption and opening paragraph. The institution identifies the ceremony and the inauguration by President Belisario Porras on 1 September 1924.

Ficha P1405, Antiguo Hospital Gorgas, Calle Gorgas y Calle Juan de Arco Galindo, Ancón, records 659775.38 E, 990772.36 N in WGS84 / UTM zone 17N, converted to 8.96024° N, 79.54667° W. Marks the hospital complex as rebuilt from 1915 to 1919. For the continuity of the French hospital site see Escobar, p. CXLIX, and MINSA. Individual wards and earlier pavilions are not fixed by this point.

June 2022 table, region 2, entry no. 788, Plaza de La Catedral, San Felipe, 8.95276° N, 79.53502° W. Square-level location. For the January circular the square is an orientation point near the contemporary legation. The July hydrant ceremony is explicitly placed in the square by the Panamanian fire brigade.

Ficha P0410, Edificio Hospital Santo Tomás y sus jardines, Calidonia, Avenida Balboa between calles 34 and 37 Este. WGS84 / UTM 17N 661372.55 E, 991793.16 N, converted to 8.96942° N, 79.53211° W. Historical description gives separate buildings, sidewalks and gardens and identifies the broad eaves.

Chapter XVI, “Malaria Work and the Hospital System”, printed p. 226, paragraph beginning “The nursing force was composed”. Gorgas describes the Black maids and orderlies who worked in the French hospital, including direct care and manual work under the sisters’ supervision.

1 May 2024, opening four paragraphs, fig. 1 and Main findings. May–December 2023 rainfall near the Gatún catchment, lake levels, ship number and size restrictions, rising urban demand and leakage, influence of El Niño, differing station trends and insufficient evidence for attribution of observed drying to human-caused warming.

summary.de: John Barrett meldete am 20. Januar, vier Arbeiter des Sanitätsdienstes würden noch wegen Gelbfiebers behandelt. Sie gehörten zu den 18 seit Juli 1904 gemeldeten Fällen. Der Platz dient zur Orientierung in der Nähe der Gesandtschaft.
summary.en: John Barrett reported on 20 January that four sanitary labourers were still in hospital with yellow fever. They were among the eighteen cases reported since July 1904. The square marks the vicinity of the legation.

summary.de: In Panama-Stadt floss Wasser aus dem oberen Río Grande durch die neuen Leitungen. Die Feuerwehr überliefert die Einweihung der Hydranten auf dem Kathedralplatz und einen späteren Brand, bei dem sie noch Zisternen nutzte.
summary.en: Water from the upper Río Grande entered Panama City’s new mains. The fire brigade records the opening of the hydrant system in Cathedral Square and a subsequent fire at which it still used cisterns.

labels.en: August 1919 · Visiting hours in Ward Nine

summary.de: Im Aufnahmevermerk steht „Spanish“. Der Besuchsplan nennt 39 Betten für Männer, die als weiß und ausländisch eingestuft wurden. Die Angehörigen hatten in diesem Teil des Krankenhauses anderthalb Stunden Besuchszeit.
summary.en: The print labels the ward “Spanish”. The visiting schedule lists thirty-nine beds for men classified as white and foreign. Families had a ninety-minute visiting period on the designated days in this part of the hospital.

labels.de: 1. September 1924 · Einweihung des Hospital Santo Tomás in Calidonia
labels.en: 1 September 1924 · Hospital Santo Tomás opens in Calidonia

summary.de: Präsident Porras eröffnete den Neubau des panamaischen Krankenhauses auf dem früheren Ausstellungsgelände. Sein Dekret vom 2. September erklärte das von der Nation errichtete Haus für den öffentlichen Dienst eröffnet.
summary.en: President Porras inaugurated the Panamanian hospital’s new buildings on the former exhibition grounds. His decree of 2 September declared the hospital built by the nation open for public service.

summary.de: Ordensschwestern, Pflegerinnen und Angehörige sorgten für die Kranken am Panamakanal. Ein Wasserkrug, eine Gelbfiebermeldung und der Besuchsplan von Ancón erzählen, was das für Familien in Panama bedeutete.
summary.en: Sisters, nurses and relatives cared for the sick on the isthmus. A household water jar, a yellow fever circular and the visiting hours at Ancón show what that meant for families in Panama.

sourceRefs.locator: pp. 51–53, Phase E and Fig. 3.2: c. 4100–3800 BCE, central mound and discrete pottery scatters
pp. 52–54, Phase F and Fig. 3.3: c. 3800–3300 BCE, estimated extent, expanded clusters and reduced spaces
Uruk management plan, Section III, pp. 56–58, and Stone Cone Building and Plan 2.7: construction, walls and stone cones
pp. 82–84, Period VIA: complex, storerooms, clay sealings and distribution vessels

summary.de: Scherben zeigen, wie sich mehrere Siedlungskerne ausdehnten.
summary.en: Pottery shows how several clusters of settlement expanded.

labels.en: Uruk · a courtyard with stone mosaics

summary.de: Ein Rest der Wanddekoration verrät, wie aufwendig Menschen im Zentrum bauten.
summary.en: Fragments of wall decoration reveal the care people put into building at the centre.

summary.de: Gefäße, Abdrücke in Ton und die Lage der Räume geben Einblick in eine zentrale Vorratshaltung.
summary.en: Vessels, clay impressions and the position of rooms give clues to centralised storage.

summary.de: Scherben in Tell Brak, ein Mosaik in Uruk und Vorratsräume in Arslantepe zeigen verschiedene Seiten des frühen Städtewachstums. Ansichtsfenster 4200–3000 v. Chr.
summary.en: Sherds at Tell Brak, a mosaic at Uruk and storerooms at Arslantepe show different sides of early urban growth. Viewing window 4200–3000 BCE.

description.de: Frühe Städte, Fernhandel und Aufzeichnungen zwischen etwa 4600 und 1800 v. Chr. Die Kapitel vergleichen zeitlich und regional unterschiedliche Entwicklungen.
description.en: Early cities, long-distance exchange and record-keeping from about 4600 to 1800 BCE. The chapters compare developments across different times and regions.

sourceRefs.locator: Site 3733, opening paragraphs on Mujir al-Din, the burial in 1398 and the reuse of the palace in 1552. Description of the ground floor, cemetery across the street and subsequent additions.
Introduction pp. 1–3, translation of the foundation conditions and map I.1 of the kitchen on the lane above al-Wad. Chapter 2, pp. 39–70, especially pp. 46–65 on revenues, employees and provisioning.

Journal of Interdisciplinary History 35.3, pp. 485–487 with note 8. The Jerusalem menu, the night before Friday, portions and the order in which the staff, residents and poor ate. DOI 10.1162/0022195052564252. Author’s accessible copy.
Inventory 2192. Description, provenance and colophon, AH 964. Fol. 1a for the tuğra, 9b–10a for the Jerusalem buildings, 12a–14b for expenditure, 49a for the founder’s seal and witnesses.
Lod, Lydda, Diospolis 1, p. 4 (site, Israel Grid 19125/65282), pp. 8–10 with figs. 3–4 and table 1 (1552 shares and 1596/97 survey), pp. 11–12 (December 1606, Jerusalem sijill 84:27).
Zeitschrift des Deutschen Palästina-Vereins 139.2, pp. 258–289. Author manuscript §§1–2, 195 names in the endowment deed, entries for al-Ludd and Bayt Iksā and its field.
Opening pages of inventory 2192. File description, 1244 × 1024 and public-domain reproduction statement.
HassekiSultanImaret3.JPG, own photograph, 6 April 2011. File details and CC0 dedication. The photograph documents the interior in 2011.

summary.de: 1398 wurde Sitt Tunshuq ihrem Jerusalemer Palast gegenüber bestattet. Im 16. Jahrhundert nahm Hürrems Stiftung die ältere Residenz in ihren Komplex auf.
summary.en: Sitt Tunshuq was buried opposite her Jerusalem palace in 1398. Hürrem’s foundation later incorporated the older residence into its complex.

summary.de: Die Urkunde von 1552 nennt Dörfer, Fluren und Anteile der Stiftung bei Lydda. In Jindās bestanden die Ansprüche mehrerer Stiftungen nebeneinander.
summary.en: The 1552 deed lists villages, tracts of farmland and shares in the district of Lydda. Several endowments had claims on income from Jindās.

summary.de: Hürrems Stiftungsbuch aus Istanbul nennt die Gebäude und die Ausgaben für Löhne und Reinigung. Der Kolophon datiert die Handschrift auf 964 AH.
summary.en: Hürrem’s foundation charter from Istanbul names the buildings and specifies spending on wages and cleaning. Its colophon dates it to AH 964.

summary.de: Die Stiftungsbestimmungen von 1557 sehen für zwei Arme zusammen eine Kelle Suppe vor. Personal und Herbergsgäste erhielten andere Portionen.
summary.en: The foundation terms of 1557 allowed two poor people one ladle of soup between them. Employees and hostel guests had different portions.

labels.en: 1606 · Four farmers put a figure on the cotton harvest

summary.de: Im Dezember 1606 kamen die Ernterechte in Jindās vor ein Jerusalemer Gericht. Vier Bauern korrigierten die Angaben zum Ertrag. Die Karte zeigt das Dorf.
summary.en: In December 1606 a Jerusalem court heard a dispute over cotton at Jindās. Four growers corrected the reported yield. The map marks their village.

summary.de: Eine Stiftungsurkunde, ein Speiseplan und vier Baumwollbauern erklären, wie aus Einnahmen palästinensischer Dörfer Brot und Suppe für Jerusalem wurden.
summary.en: An endowment charter, a menu and four cotton growers show how income from Palestinian villages helped provide bread and soup in Jerusalem.

sourceRefs.locator: “The birthplace of Christianity in Scotland” and “Columba’s monastery”. Foundation tradition of 563, timber-building evidence, the later church and the eighth- and ninth-century crosses.
Location and national grid reference NM 28683 24515 for the abbey site.
Source Description, Primary Manuscripts no. 1. Schaffhausen Stadtbibliothek, Generalia 1, colophon p. 136a, the two-column copy and the likely date before 713.
Origin and Provenance. Dorbbéne’s prayer on p. 136 and the partly erased Reichenau ex-libris at the foot of p. 1.
Early Medieval England and its Neighbours 51, e6, pp. 1–3, especially n. 5. Medieval Welsh identities, and Brittonic and Goidelic as modern linguistic terms.

“Marginalia”, first and second memoranda. Gelhi, Cingal, the horse, the altar of Teilo, the disputed land and the case for Llandeilo Fawr. Eighth-century main text and a mid-ninth-century dating suggested for the first two additions.
Section on the Lichfield Gospels. The editor favours the early ninth century for the gift, and identifies Llandeilo Fawr as probable. The station therefore uses the ninth century as a window.
pp. 85–124, opening comparison with Wales, especially Chad document no. 4. Ris, a land grant, its bounds and dues.
Site Record, grid reference SN6293022236 for the later church at Llandeilo. The identification of the earlier altar is probable.

Section 2.1.3, “Viking and Norman Dublin”. The two early settlements south of the river, a pool of the Poddle, and a Liffey crossing. Modern city centre used only to orient the probable building region.
Chapter 5.2, printed pp. 183–186, especially the keelson’s incomplete 104th ring on p. 184, the repair sequence and the summary on pp. 185–186; fig. 55 compares excavated Dublin ship parts.
First three paragraphs, covering crew, oak, tentative origin in the Dublin area around 1042, and 60 oars.
Paragraphs on High Street and Dublin excavations, especially textile production, spindles, loom weights, yarn and surviving shoes and bags.
Introduction and Physical Description. Tenth-century Gospel text, Gaelic additions on ff. 3–5, the Latin brieve on f. 40, and the 155 × 110 mm parchment codex.
In Ì Chaluim Chille, pp. 383–415. Discussion of Bishop Cormac and Book of Deer no. III, notes 53–54. Gartnait and Éte’s grant, the pledge, and dating between April 1131 and April 1132.

Opening paragraphs and the 2022 excavation. The team proposes a site about 80 metres from the later Deer Abbey near Mintlaw. The map gives the district rather than pinpointing the grant or place of writing.
Description, photograph date (16 February 2004), photographer, original JPG and source licensing section, CC BY-SA 2.0 Germany. The visible timber fragments occupy the foreground metal frame.

labels.de: 563 nach der Überlieferung · Columbas Gemeinschaft auf Iona
labels.en: 563 in the foundation tradition · Columba’s community on Iona

summary.de: Der Überlieferung zufolge kam Columba mit Gefährten aus Irland. Der heutige Kirchenbau ist jünger. Bei der frühen Gemeinschaft sind Spuren von Holzbauten erhalten.
summary.en: Tradition puts the arrival of Columba and companions from Ireland in this year. The present church is later. Archaeology has identified timber buildings belonging to the early community.

labels.de: 9. Jahrhundert · Wie ein Buch an den Altar kam
labels.en: 9th century · How a book came to the altar

summary.de: Gelhi gab sein bestes Pferd für das Buch und schenkte es der Kirche des heiligen Teilo. Andere Einträge sprechen für Llandeilo Fawr als Ort der Schenkung.
summary.en: Gelhi bought the book with his best horse and gave it to the church of St Teilo. Other entries favour Llandeilo Fawr as the place of the gift.

summary.de: Der Baum für die Maststütze wurde im Mai oder Juni 1042 gefällt. Das Schiff wurde damals oder bald darauf in Ostirland gebaut, wahrscheinlich im Raum Dublin. Die Karte zeigt die Region der vermuteten Werft.
summary.en: The oak for the keelson was felled in May or June 1042. The ship was built then or soon afterwards in eastern Ireland, probably around Dublin. The map locates the likely region of the yard.

labels.de: April 1131 bis April 1132 · Éte und Gartnait geben Land
labels.en: April 1131 to April 1132 · Éte and Gartnait grant land

summary.de: Eine gälische Notiz überliefert ihre Schenkung und eine Sicherheit an Bischof Cormac. Die Karte verortet die Gemeinschaft von Deer, für die der Eintrag bestimmt war.
summary.en: A Gaelic note records their grant and a pledge to Bishop Cormac. The map locates the community at Deer that the record concerned.

summary.de: Auf Iona, in Wales und in Buchan bewahrten Bücher Namen und Rechte. In Dublin führt das Holz eines Langschiffs zu den Menschen an der Irischen See.
summary.en: Books on Iona, in Wales and in Buchan preserved names and rights. In Dublin the timber of a longship leads to the people who worked around the Irish Sea.

sourceRefs.locator: Hull and rowing holes, the ship built in 820, burial of two women in 834 and the uncertainty over their identities and status.

“The Jelling Stone”, translated inscription and photographs. The museum dates the raising to c. 965. Harald’s parents and claims about Denmark, Norway and Christianity, earlier Christian objects and Harald Klak’s baptism at Mainz in 826.

“Gorm the Old authored Denmark’s name certificate” and “Two monuments from Danish history”. Gorm’s commissioning formula, the museum’s rendering of Thyra’s epithet, c. 950, and the photograph “The small Jelling stone” by Roberto Fortuna, CC BY-SA 2.0.
Geographical data table, property 697bis, N55° 45′ 23″ E9° 25′ 12″.

Antiquity 97, 1262–1278. Table 1, introduction on the north mound, “Ravnunge-Tue and the Jelling stones”, figures 9–10, “Sources of error” and conclusion. Læborg’s signed dedication and proposed attribution of Jelling 2, weathering at Jelling 1, variants of Thyra’s epithet, and limits of the proposed reburial. The authors give 959/60 for wood from the chamber.

Abstract of chapter 12 in Jelling – Monuments and Landscape, pp. 313–332. The smaller stone is no longer in its original position. Excavation during protection works in 2011 re-examined the central area and the position of the larger stone.

Danish Journal of Archaeology 3(2), pp. 168–170, tables 1–2 and discussion immediately after table 2. Mid-tenth century up to c. 960 for Jelling 1. The chamber wood is reported as 958/59. Historical dating proposals for Jelling 2 differ.

Figures 2–6 and English summary under “Stone for his parents” and “Small silver cup”. Vertical and horizontal writing, reliefs, purple silk, and the 4.3 cm silver cup with gilding and entwined animals from the north mound.
Object DO-1525. Description of the west-facing section and view of the burial chamber (Tabula I, 1823); Placering / Koordinater 55.75704, 9.41993. Location reference only.

“The palisade”, “The timber buildings” and “The rune-stones and burial mounds”, pp. 6–7. Area of 12.7 ha, oak planks and paired round posts, trench depth 1–1.2 m, traces of three buildings, southeastern wetland wood and estimate 958–985, probably around 968.

16 August 2013, paragraphs on the sampling by Niels Bonde and the Smededammen excavation. Eleven of twelve samples dated; one preserved wood immediately inside the bark. The 1.4 km circuit and most probable date around 968.
Record DO-6476 identifies the pond as Smededammen. Placering / Koordinater 55.75584, 9.42238, approximate orientation at the pond, not the exact sampled plank.

“Danmarks længste bro i tusind år” and “En imponerende konstruktion”. Measurements and construction, wood joints, variable post lengths, suggested traffic, local attribution to Harald and conventional date c. 980.

KUML 52, figs 1 and 3; Danish discussion on pp. 216 and 220–221 and the English conclusion pp. 224–225. The last identified ring yields autumn 979 as a lower limit. Missing bark and revised sapwood statistics give a felling range of roughly 980–1010.
Q996217, coordinate location P625, 55°40′16.4″ N, 9°20′46.9″ E. Approximate site orientation.

Aarbøger for Nordisk Oldkyndighed og Historie 1982 (issued 1984), pp. 111–152. Figure 8 and the English results and conclusion on pp. 145–147: four June/July felling estimates for timbers of the inner ditch barrier; D 701 from the outer bridge, August 980 to May 981; what these can date directly.
Section “Trelleborg”, plan and text. Sixteen houses inside the rampart, cemetery with at least 157 men, women and children, and an alternative association with the village 200 metres away.

Advisory-body evaluation, “Brief description” and statement of Outstanding Universal Value. Danish fortresses with broadly shared geometric layout and four gates, attribution during Harald’s reign and interpretive limits on their purpose.
Geographical data, component 1660-004, Trelleborg in Zealand. Central point 55°23′39″ N, 11°15′55″ E and property maps.

labels.de: Königin Thyra und die Bauleute von Jelling
labels.en: Queen Thyra and the builders of Jelling

summary.de: Gorm lässt seiner Frau Thyra einen Stein setzen. Die Karte markiert den heutigen Standort in Jelling. Der ursprüngliche Aufstellungsort ist ungewiss.
summary.en: Gorm commissions a stone for his wife Thyra. The map shows its present location at Jelling. Its original position is uncertain.

labels.de: um 959 · Ein Silberbecher aus der Grabkammer
labels.en: around 959 · A silver cup from the burial chamber

summary.de: Holz aus der Kammer im Nordhügel ist um 959 datiert. Ein kleiner verzierter Becher und Seidenreste sind erhalten. Wer hier bestattet war, bleibt offen.
summary.en: Wood from the North Mound chamber dates to about 959. A decorated cup and scraps of silk survive. The identity of the person or people buried here is uncertain.

labels.de: um 965 · Haralds Stein und die Hand des Runenmeisters
labels.en: around 965 · Harald’s stone and the carver’s hand

summary.de: Harald gedenkt seiner Eltern und beansprucht die Christianisierung der Dänen für sich. Die Rillen der Schrift legen nahe, dass Ravnunge-Tue die Runen schlug.
summary.en: Harald commemorates his parents and claims credit for the conversion of the Danes. The carved grooves suggest that Ravnunge-Tue cut the inscription.

labels.en: probably around 968 · Oak planks at Smededammen

summary.de: Von zwölf Proben aus der Palisade ließen sich elf datieren. Die Spanne für das Fällen reicht von 958 bis 985, am wahrscheinlichsten ist 968. Der Punkt zeigt den Bereich des heutigen Teichs.
summary.en: Eleven of twelve samples from the palisade could be dated. Felling falls between 958 and 985, most probably around 968. The point marks the area of the present pond.

labels.de: etwa 980–1010 · Eine Holzbrücke über die Talwiesen
labels.en: roughly 980–1010 · A timber bridge across the valley

summary.de: Die Pfosten markieren eine etwa 760 Meter lange Brücke. Der jüngste gemessene Ring stammt von 979. Ohne erhaltene Rinde bleibt der Fällzeitpunkt ungefähr auf 980 bis 1010 eingegrenzt.
summary.en: Timber posts mark a bridge roughly 760 metres long. The latest ring measured dates to 979. With bark missing, felling can be placed only broadly around 980–1010.

labels.en: 980–981 · Two ditches at one building site

summary.de: Hölzer aus der Sperre im inneren Graben und von der Brücke über den äußeren belegen Bauarbeiten 980/81. Der Punkt zeigt die Ringburg bei Slagelse auf Seeland.
summary.en: Timbers from the inner ditch barrier and the bridge over the outer ditch place construction in 980–981. The point marks the ring fortress near Slagelse, Zealand.

summary.de: Wer schlug die Runen zum Gedenken an Thyra? An zwei Steinen lässt sich die Hand eines Handwerkers verfolgen. Kammerhölzer, die Palisade am Dorfteich und zwei große Bauwerke erzählen von der Arbeit für die Könige von Jelling.
summary.en: Who cut the runes in memory of Thyra? The hand of a craftsperson can be traced across two stones. Chamber timbers, the palisade at a village pond and two great building sites reveal work on the scale of the Jelling kings.

sourceRefs.locator: Table 1 and pp. 614–615, Figs. 6–7: architectural phases of the Western Deffufa and its religious quarter.
Description, paragraphs on the capital of Kush and goods, pottery and seal impressions connected with exchange.
Table 1; pp. 12 and 15–16, Ceramic assemblage and Figs. 2, 4: fabrics, manufacturing styles and cooking sherd counts.
p. 113, Stela of Sepedher 10984, room 13; surviving lines 6–9, office and temple building for ruler of Kush.
Finding place, Current location and Dating; late Second Intermediate Period and 17th Dynasty.
pp. 143–146, §1.1, the Buhen inscriptions and the debate over the word read as Nedjeh.
Note, location on the west bank and present submergence beneath the reservoir.

summary.de: Die Westliche Deffufa lag im religiösen Viertel einer nubischen Hauptstadt.
summary.en: The Western Deffufa stood in the religious quarter of a Nubian capital.

summary.de: Ruß und Gefäßformen zeigen, welche Töpfe Menschen in der Festung zum Kochen verwendeten.
summary.en: Soot and vessel shapes show what kinds of pots people used to cook in the fortress.

summary.de: Eine Stele verbindet ein lokales Amt mit dem Herrscher von Kusch.
summary.en: A stela connects a local office with the ruler of Kush.

summary.de: Ein Tempel, Kochscherben und eine Stele erzählen vom Königreich Kerma und seinen Nachbarn am Nil.
summary.en: A temple, cooking sherds and a stela tell the story of the Kingdom of Kerma and its neighbours along the Nile.

description.de: Handel, Diplomatie, Werkstätten und Herrschaft zwischen etwa 1800 und 1000 v. Chr. Die Kapitel folgen den jeweils regionalen Datierungen und vergleichen konkrete Funde.
description.en: Trade, diplomacy, workshops and power from roughly 1800 to 1000 BCE. The chapters follow local chronologies and compare specific finds.

sourceRefs.locator: Editorial introduction on the sixteenth-century copies of the Latin text; heading and articles I (chosen citizens), V (houses, vineyards and avenues for complaint) and VIII (officers entitled to seize goods, working cattle and field labourers).
Manuscript, complete digitisation; Descripción. Colophon naming Seville and 1283, Arabic sources for games, chess, dice and tables, representations of women, men and the monarch playing.
Datos técnicos and Descripción. Castilian text, 97 parchment leaves, tilted boards displaying actual positions, women and men playing and the range of cultural backgrounds shown by the illuminators.
Opening four paragraphs. Work on the palace began in the late 1370s or early 1380s; the twelve-sided basin, the inscription of Ibn Zamrak’s verses, and differences between the lions’ faces and tails.
Poema de la Fuente de los Leones. Ibn Zamrak’s eulogy of the sultan, garden and fountain inscribed in its white marble basin.
Courtyard, fountain and central cylinder balancing water inflow and outflow; palace in Muhammad V’s second reign, 1362–1391.

Collection MHJ035. 10 July 1492, leaders of Girona’s Jewish community, cathedral canons, sale for 300 lliures made under Ferdinand’s expulsion order. Latin parchment in Girona Municipal Archive; related deeds sewn into a 3.6-metre roll of eleven documents.
Opening paragraphs: the last medieval synagogue of Girona was built in 1435 on the site now occupied by the museum and used until 1492.
Chapter 1, Historical Setting, Ferdinand and Isabella. The personal union and the continuing separate political institutions in Castile, Aragon, Catalonia and Valencia.

Opening paragraph on the commemorative plaque at Pino Suárez and República de El Salvador, the comparison of possible locations and the concluding identification of the southern approach to Tenochtitlan, 8 November 1519.
Second letter to Charles, excerpt pp. 85–89. Bridge and removable beams; attendants prevent physical contact; later speech in the lodging as reported to Charles.

Book XII, chapter 16. Opening place-names, garlands and necklaces, Moteuczoma’s welcome, Marina interpreting the answer, and the list of the lords accompanying Moteuczoma. This English excerpt presents the later Nahua account.
Bibliographic note Segunda Carta. The letter is dated 30 October 1520 in Segura de la Frontera; first printed at Seville in 1522.

labels.de: Von den Spieltischen in Sevilla bis zum Brief an Karl
labels.en: From the gaming tables of Seville to a letter for Charles

labels.de: 1188 · Bürger in der Versammlung von León
labels.en: 1188 · Townspeople at the gathering in León

summary.de: Alfons IX. ließ in León die Beteiligung gewählter Bürger und Regeln zum Schutz von Häusern, Weinbergen und Zugvieh festhalten. Der Punkt markiert die Stadt.
summary.en: At León, Alfonso IX recorded the participation of chosen citizens and provisions for protecting homes, vineyards and working cattle. The marker locates the city.

summary.de: Der Schlussvermerk nennt Sevilla als Ort, an dem das Buch der Spiele 1283 begonnen und vollendet wurde.
summary.en: The colophon identifies Seville as the city where the Book of Games was begun and completed in 1283.

labels.de: Um 1380 · Ein Palasthof für Muhammad V.
labels.en: Around 1380 · A palace courtyard for Muhammad V

summary.de: Der Sultan ließ um 1380 mit dem Bau beginnen. Ibn Zamraks Gedicht steht am Becken des Löwenbrunnens. Der Beginn der Arbeiten ist nur ungefähr datiert.
summary.en: The sultan initiated construction around 1380. Ibn Zamrak’s poem is inscribed on the fountain basin. The start of the works can only be dated approximately.

summary.de: Nach Ferdinands Ausweisungsbefehl verkauften Gemeindevertreter am 10. Juli die Synagogenräume an die Domherren von Girona.
summary.en: On 10 July, following Ferdinand’s expulsion order, community representatives sold the synagogue premises to the canons of Girona Cathedral.

labels.de: 1519 · Ein Empfang im Brief an Karl
labels.en: 1519 · A welcome in the letter to Charles

summary.de: Cortés schildert die Begegnung mit Moteuczoma II. im zweiten Brief an Karl. Die Karte zeigt den südlichen Zugang zur Stadt als ungefähre Ortsangabe.
summary.en: In his second letter to Charles, Cortés described meeting Moteuczoma II. The southern approach to the city is shown as a general location.

summary.de: Bürger in León, Schachspieler in Sevilla, ein Dichter in Granada und die jüdische Gemeinde von Girona hinterließen ganz verschiedene Texte. Cortés’ Brief führt zur Nahua-Überlieferung derselben Begegnung.
summary.en: Citizens of León, chess players in Seville, a poet in Granada and the Jewish community of Girona left very different texts. A letter from Cortés leads to a Nahua account of the same encounter.

sourceRefs.locator: Introduction, opening discussion of Bede, Ecclesiastical History I.1, British and English, and the changing languages of Britain.
Introduction and description of f. 128v, lines 1–4: Bede completed the History in 731; early copy and three lines of Northumbrian verse in the main scribe’s hand.
Book IV, chapter 24, opening narrative and verses: the feast, animals at Whitby, the dream, the Latin rendering of the English hymn.
National Heritage List for England 1002978, Location, National Grid Reference NZ 33870 65184.

Scope and Content, post-Gospel additions: 51 records of manumission in Latin and Old English, marginal and blank-leaf entries. The catalogue’s broad dating should be read with Pracy’s discussion of individual hands and names.
Printed p. 627, entry beginning Her kyð on þissere bec. Old English text and translation: Ongynethel and Gythiccael, half a pound, four pence, two officials, church door and altar, named witnesses.
The Haskins Society Journal 31, pp. 1 and 9, especially notes 40–43. Competing datings for entries sharing the name Maccos, around 1000 or late in the eleventh century.
National Heritage List for England 1355166, Location and Details, grid SX 07313 67033. The standing church is later than the entry and is used to locate Bodmin only.
Latin palaeography, Lesson One, E 31/1/3, folios 311v–312, text lines 1–11 and English translation. Land, burgesses, men described as French and the gift of 60,000 herrings.
Location, map and History. The later friary stood at the western edge of the medieval town. The Domesday section gives 236 burgesses and the land already lost to coastal erosion.
Edition and comparison of the Huntingdonshire and Oxfordshire texts; address to clergy and laity, majority of councillors, open sealed writ to be kept locally and final dating at London.

Chapter on the reform period, printed pp. 38–40, especially p. 39 nn. 1–2 and p. 40 n. 2. The 18 October letter, English and French witnesses, Burton annalist’s Latin version and a payment of 50s to Robert of Fulham on 7 November for work in English and French.
Coordinates and historical-geography note for the medieval City. A town-level reference only.

labels.de: Ein Lied, eine Freilassung und 60.000 Heringe
labels.en: A song, a manumission and 60,000 herrings

summary.de: Der Mönch beendet in Wearmouth-Jarrow seine lateinische Geschichte. Die Karte zeigt den Klosterstandort Jarrow. Eine frühe Abschrift bewahrt Cædmons Lied zusätzlich in altenglischer Sprache.
summary.en: Bede completes his Latin history at Wearmouth-Jarrow. The map marks the Jarrow monastery site. An early copy also preserves Cædmon’s hymn in Old English.

labels.de: Um 1000 oder später im 11. Jahrhundert · Ongynethel und Gythiccael werden freigelassen
labels.en: Around 1000 or later in the eleventh century · Ongynethel and Gythiccael obtain their freedom

summary.de: Eine altenglische Notiz nennt den Kauf an der Kirchentür und die Freilassung am Altar. Die Zuordnung des Zeugen Maccos lässt einen weiten Datierungsspielraum. Der Punkt bezeichnet Bodmin.
summary.en: An Old English entry records a purchase at the church door and a manumission at the altar. The identification of the witness Maccos leaves a wide dating window. The point locates Bodmin.

labels.de: 1086 · Dunwich wird für das Domesday Book erfasst
labels.en: 1086 · Dunwich is recorded in Domesday Book

summary.de: Der Eintrag für das Gut nennt Landverluste an das Meer, einen Wechsel der Grundherrschaft und eine Gabe in Heringen. Der Punkt liegt an der heutigen Küste beim größtenteils untergegangenen Ort.
summary.en: The entry describes coastal erosion, a change of lordship and a gift of herrings. The point is on the modern shore beside the largely submerged medieval town.

labels.de: 18. Oktober 1258 · Heinrichs III. Schreiben an die Grafschaften
labels.en: 18 October 1258 · Henry III’s letter to the shires

summary.de: Ein in London ausgestelltes Schreiben verpflichtet den König auf die Beschlüsse seiner Räte. Zwei englische Fassungen lassen die Adressaten erkennen.
summary.en: A writ issued in London commits the king to his councillors’ decisions. The addressees can still be discerned in two English versions.

summary.de: Beda überliefert ein Lied aus Whitby, in Bodmin gewinnt eine Familie ihre Freiheit, und für Dunwich zählt ein Schreiber Heringe. In vier Quellen begegnen dir die Menschen und die Sprachen des mittelalterlichen England.
summary.en: Bede preserves a song from Whitby, a family gains its freedom in Bodmin, and Dunwich owes a gift in herrings. Four records take us among the people and languages of medieval England.

sourceRefs.locator: Object Information and overview: accession, approximate date, probable Amarna provenance, clay, dimensions, Assyrian Akkadian and proposed addressee

summary.de: Eine kleine Tontafel nennt einen Boten, einen Wagen, zwei Pferde und Lapislazuli.
summary.en: A small clay tablet names a messenger, a chariot, two horses and lapis lazuli.

summary.de: Keilschriftfragmente bewahren das Abkommen zwischen Ramses II. und Hattusili III.
summary.en: Cuneiform fragments preserve the agreement between Ramesses II and Hattusili III.

summary.de: Die Hieroglyphen an der Tempelwand beschreiben auch das Siegel der Königin Puduḫepa.
summary.en: The hieroglyphs on the temple wall also describe Queen Puduḫepa’s seal.

summary.de: Ein Bote mit Geschenken, Vertragsabschriften auf Ton und eine Tempelwand zeigen, wie Königshöfe Beziehungen pflegten.
summary.en: A messenger bearing gifts, copies on clay and a temple wall show how royal courts managed their relationships.

description.de: Handel, Diplomatie, Werkstätten und Herrschaft zwischen etwa 1800 und 1000 v. Chr. Die Kapitel folgen den jeweils regionalen Datierungen und vergleichen konkrete Funde.
description.en: Trade, diplomacy, workshops and power from roughly 1800 to 1000 BCE. The chapters follow local chronologies and compare specific finds.

labels.en: Living at the Edge of the Ice

summary.de: Ein großer Mammutknochenkreis und Spuren von Feuer. Ob dort ein Haus stand, bleibt offen.
summary.en: A large mammoth-bone circle and traces of fire. Whether a house stood here remains open.

summary.de: Vergleiche im Grabungsplan die dunklen Hüttenbefunde mit den helleren Feuerstellen und dem Fünf-Meter-Maßstab.
summary.en: Compare the dark hut features with the paler hearths and the five-metre scale on the excavation plan.

summary.de: In der heute trockenen Landschaft lag damals zeitweise ein Feuchtgebiet. Ein Hüttenboden zeigt, wie klein eine Unterkunft sein konnte.
summary.en: Today’s dry landscape once included a wetland. A hut floor shows how small a shelter could be.

summary.de: Wie bauten Menschen in der letzten Kaltzeit? Ein Mammutknochenkreis am Don, Hütten am See Genezareth und wiederholte Aufenthalte im heutigen Jordanien. Ansichtsfenster 30.000–18.800 Jahre BP.
summary.en: How did people build during the last glacial period? A mammoth-bone circle on the Don, huts beside the Sea of Galilee and repeated stays in present-day Jordan. Viewing window 30,000–18,800 years BP.

description.de: Gemeinsamer Suchbereich für die frühen Kapitel der Menschheitsgeschichte. Regionale Einteilungen und Datierungen unterscheiden sich; die Kapitel können sich zeitlich überlappen. Ihre Zeitspannen stehen jeweils am Kapitel.
description.en: A shared discovery group for the early chapters of human history. Regional period definitions and dates differ; chapters can overlap in time. Each chapter shows its own time span.

sourceRefs.locator: pp. 220–223, figs. 1–2 and n. 4. Two neighbouring sites and more than 1,300 graves used from the final third of the fifth century to the end of the seventh.
Project description, cemetery plan and photograph caption for grave 90. A disc brooch and beads from a necklace at chest level, first half of the seventh century.
Opening paragraphs and excavation plan. Settlement traces, sixth to eleventh centuries, 200 metres downslope from the cemetery. Both surface buildings and sunken buildings are documented.
pp. 20–21, figs. 1, 3–5. Seventh-century evidence and several superimposed dwellings, longhouses interpreted as byre-dwellings, clay loom weights from sunken buildings.
pp. 222–224, 231, figs. 3–4. Successive houses, few datable finds from postholes, sixth-century material and the long life of the settlement.
pp. 296–297, discussion of the genitium, screona and sunken buildings. Textile tools frequently occur in secondary fills. Single-purpose and gendered interpretations require further evidence.

pp. 179–181, opening counts and fig. 1. 22,155 beads in the cemetery; individual groups range from a few beads to more than 300. Section on Mosaikperlen and Millefioriperlen explains cross-cut patterned glass canes.
pp. 298–302, figs. 4a–c. Reconstructed successive fence lines in the south-eastern sector. Phase II encloses four graves, including graves 24 and 25 dated to the last third of the seventh century.

Publisher’s description, paragraphs beginning “In direkter Nachbarschaft” and “200 Meter entfernt”. The completed catalogue records 86 burials in small cemeteries adjoining six farmsteads around AD 700.
pp. 227–231, figs. 5, 6 and 9, n. 12. Waterlogged graves at the eastern farm, winter 703/704 felling date for freshly worked oak of grave 27, and the excavator’s dating of the burial to early 704.

Object data and Beschreibung, inventory 1989-0011-0769-9000. Mortised bed, wooden dowels and wedge, single bottom board, red and black decoration, leather and plant fibres, and gables added for the burial.
Objektfotografie and Copyright → Hauptbild for inventory 1989-0011-0769-9000. The holding museum licenses its main image under CC BY-SA 4.0. No individual photographer is credited on the record.

labels.de: Spätes 5. Jh. · Ein Friedhof am Hang
labels.en: Late 5th century · A burial ground on the slope

summary.de: 485 steht hier für das letzte Drittel des fünften Jahrhunderts, in das die frühesten Gräber datieren.
summary.en: 485 represents the final third of the fifth century, the archaeological date of the earliest graves.

summary.de: 550 ist ein Lesejahr für die Siedlungsspuren des sechsten Jahrhunderts. Die einzelnen Neubauten haben unterschiedliche und meist viel gröbere Datierungen.
summary.en: 550 is a viewing year for the sixth-century settlement evidence. Individual rebuilds have different and usually much broader dates.

labels.de: Frühes 7. Jh. · Eine Halskette in Grab 90
labels.en: Early 7th century · A necklace in grave 90

summary.de: 625 steht für die erste Hälfte des siebten Jahrhunderts. In Grab 90 lagen im Brustbereich eine Fibel und Kettenperlen.
summary.en: 625 represents the first half of the seventh century. A brooch and necklace beads were found at chest level in grave 90.

labels.de: Spätes 7. Jh. · Gräber innerhalb des Hofzauns
labels.en: Late 7th century · Burials inside the farmyard fence

summary.de: 685 liegt im Datierungsfenster zweier Gräber, die der zweite Zaun umschloss. Sein Baujahr ist unbekannt.
summary.en: 685 falls within the dating range for two burials enclosed by the second fence. Its construction year is unknown.

summary.de: Der letzte Jahrring der frisch verarbeiteten Kammer-Eiche ergibt die Fällzeit Winter 703/704. Stork setzt die Beisetzung an den Jahresanfang 704. Das Fertigungsjahr des Betts bleibt offen.
summary.en: The outermost ring of the freshly worked chamber oak places its felling in the winter of 703/704. Stork dates the burial to early 704. The bed’s year of manufacture remains open.

summary.de: Ein Webgewicht, Perlen einer Halskette und ein ausgebessertes Bett erzählen vom Leben an der Jagst. In Mittelhofen lassen sich sogar die Zäune verfolgen, die manche Höfe nach und nach um ihre Gräber zogen.
summary.en: A loom weight, necklace beads and a repaired bed open up life on the Jagst. At Mittelhofen it is even possible to follow the changing fence lines as some farmyards began to enclose graves.

sourceRefs.locator: Sections Huitzilopochco and Desarrollo del asentamiento. Southwestern lake shore, fresh and brackish water, chinampas and neighbouring allies; in 1428 Tenochtitlan imposed tribute in goods and labour.
Overview; Key Events, ca. 1427 and ca. 1431. Tenochtitlan’s alliance with Texcoco and Tlacopan, Azcapotzalco, indirect rule, tribute and Tlaxcala’s autonomy. Earlier enlargements of the main temple.
Folio 47r. Pictorial record and colonial annotations of tribute for Xoconochco (Soconusco); rows of cacao, feathers, skins and vessels. The folio concerns a different province from Huitzilopochco.
Figure 1, p. 36. Identifies Soconusco, cacao beans, drinking vessels and jaguar skins on Codex Mendoza fol. 47r; dates the manuscript to the early colonial period.
Curator’s object description, the numeral and reed for 1487, the two rulers Tízoc and Ahuítzotl making blood offerings, the bundle between them and the probable ceremonial-square display.
Archaeological zone, Guatemala 60, Centro Histórico, and Datos generales, site of the principal building of ancient Tenochtitlan.

Opening paragraph on the commemorative plaque at Pino Suárez and República de El Salvador, the comparison of possible locations and the concluding identification of the southern approach to Tenochtitlan, 8 November 1519.

Book XII, chapter 16. Opening place-names, garlands and necklaces, Moteuczoma’s welcome, Marina interpreting the answer, and the list of the lords accompanying Moteuczoma. This English excerpt presents the later Nahua account.
Second letter to Charles, excerpt pp. 85–89. Bridge and removable beams; attendants prevent physical contact; later speech in the lodging as reported to Charles.

Opening project description. Nahua elders, authors and artists and Bernardino de Sahagún, parallel Nahuatl/Spanish text, 12 books, completion in 1577 at the Imperial Colegio de la Santa Cruz in Tlatelolco.
Discussion of the creation of the manuscript and its Nahua authors, including the four named grammarians, rector Martín Jacobita of Tlatelolco, and Antonio Valeriano of Azcapotzalco.
Tenochtitlan/Tlatelolco map, circa 1500; slide headed Images of artists/scribes (tlahcuilohqueh), Florentine Codex, Book 11 and the lists of named grammarians and scribes.

labels.en: Who supplied the island city of Tenochtitlan?

summary.de: In Huitzilopochco am südwestlichen Seeufer mussten Haushalte Tenochtitlan von 1428 an Güter und Arbeitsleistungen liefern.
summary.en: From 1428 the households of Huitzilopochco on the southwestern lake shore owed goods and labour to Tenochtitlan.

labels.en: 1487 · Eight Reed at the Great Temple

summary.de: Am Ausbau des Großen Tempels erinnert die Gedenktafel an Tízoc und Ahuítzotl. Das Jahr Acht Rohr entspricht hier 1487. Die Karte zeigt den Zeremonialbezirk.
summary.en: A commemorative plaque associates Tízoc and Ahuítzotl with the enlargement of the Great Temple. Eight Reed corresponds here to 1487. The point marks the ceremonial precinct.

labels.de: 1519 · Moteuczoma II. und Cortés am südlichen Zugang
labels.en: 1519 · Moteuczoma II and Cortés on the southern approach

summary.de: Moteuczoma II. empfing Cortés am südlichen Zugang zur Inselstadt. Der spätere Nahuatl-Bericht nennt die Beteiligten, auch Malintzin als Dolmetscherin. Die Markierung zeigt den ungefähren Ort.
summary.en: Moteuczoma II received Cortés on the southern approach to the island city. The later Nahuatl account names members of the party including Malintzin, who interpreted. The marker gives the approximate locality.

labels.de: 1577 · Die Arbeit am Florentiner Codex kommt zum Abschluss

summary.de: 1577 wurde das Werk mit seinen zwölf Büchern am Kolleg Santa Cruz vollendet. Nahua-Gelehrte und Maler hatten darin Wissen und Erinnerungen der Stadt festgehalten.
summary.en: In 1577 the twelve books were completed at the College of Santa Cruz. Nahua scholars and painters had recorded knowledge and memories of the city.

summary.de: Von den Abgaben einer Stadt am See und dem Jahr Acht Rohr bis zu Blumen für Cortés. In Tlatelolco schrieben Nahua-Gelehrte die Begrüßung aus der Sicht ihrer Stadt auf.
summary.en: A lakeside town owes tribute, two rulers mark the year Eight Reed, and a visitor receives flowers. At Tlatelolco Nahua scholars recorded the welcome from the city’s perspective.

sourceRefs.locator: Opening discussion of Rhomaioi and the capital; “The Latin Occupation of Constantinople” and “Late Byzantium” on 1204, 1261, Nicaea and Trebizond.

Opening paragraphs on the Nika fire, dedication on 27 December 537, architects, vault, 558 collapse, 562 rebuilding and decoration. Closing paragraphs on conversion under Mehmed II in 1453 and subsequent Ottoman additions.
Sultanahmet Urban Archaeological Component Area, component 356bis-001, Istanbul historic peninsula. The atlas places the church within the mapped area.

Theodora and Justinian panels, particularly embroidered Three Magi along the hem, purple garments, ceremonial vessels and retinues.
Component 788-002, Church of St. Vitale. Coordinate table and adopted map at 1:1500.

The Byzantine Harbours of Constantinople, Fig. 9 and accompanying text and note 141 on YK 12 and the proposed season of sinking.
Shipwrecks Database, entry 997: site-level coordinates 41.00447° N, 28.95249° E for Yenikapı. The point locates the excavation area, not the individual hull.
Building history, from the conversion of the patriarchal cathedral under Mehmed II in 1453 to the successive Ottoman minarets.

labels.de: Eine Kuppel, zwei Herrscherbilder und ein Korb Kirschkerne
labels.en: A dome, two imperial portraits and a basket of cherry stones

summary.de: Justinians Neubau wurde am 27. Dezember geweiht. Die erste Kuppel stürzte 558 ein.
summary.en: Justinian’s new church was dedicated on 27 December. Its first dome collapsed in 558.

summary.de: Maximian weihte San Vitale. Im Altarraum begleiten sein Name und sein Bild Justinian. Gegenüber bringt Theodora einen Kelch.
summary.en: Maximian consecrated San Vitale. In its sanctuary, his name and image accompany Justinian. Theodora carries a chalice on the opposite wall.

labels.en: 9th century · A coastal trader in the Theodosian harbour

summary.de: Münze und Amphoren stützen die Datierung des Wracks YK 12 ins neunte Jahrhundert. Der Punkt markiert das Ausgrabungsgebiet im Hafen.
summary.en: A coin and amphoras support a ninth-century date for wreck YK 12. The point identifies the harbour excavation area.

labels.de: 1453 · Die bisherige Kathedrale wird zur Moschee
labels.en: 1453 · The former cathedral becomes a mosque

summary.de: 1453 ließ Mehmed II. die Hagia Sophia als Moschee einrichten. Der Bau der alten Kathedrale blieb an seinem Platz.
summary.en: In 1453 Mehmed II had Hagia Sophia converted into a mosque. The fabric of the old cathedral remained in place.

summary.de: Unter der Kuppel der Hagia Sophia, vor den Mosaiken von Ravenna und an Bord eines Küstenschiffs begegnen uns Menschen des östlichen Römischen Reichs. Nach 1453 ändert eine Kathedrale ihre Bestimmung.
summary.en: A dome in Constantinople, two mosaics at Ravenna and a coastal ship bring the people of the eastern Roman Empire into view. In 1453 their cathedral acquired a new use.

summary.en: Layers preserve compacted dung and salts. What can the two clues together tell us about animals spending time at the site?

labels.en: Ganj Dareh · goat bones and DNA

summary.de: Alter, Geschlecht und Verwandtschaft erzählen unterschiedliche Teile derselben Geschichte. Warum kann eine gehaltene Ziege wie eine Wildziege aussehen?
summary.en: Age, sex and genetic affinity tell different parts of the story. Why might a managed goat still resemble a wild one?

summary.de: Poröser Ton kann Fett bewahren. Was verraten Kohlenstoffisotope über den früheren Inhalt eines Gefäßes?
summary.en: Porous pottery can preserve fats. What do carbon isotopes tell us about what once went into the pot?

summary.de: Dung, Ziegenknochen und Fettrückstände: Wie lassen sich die ersten Praktiken der Tierhaltung und die Nutzung von Milch erkennen? Drei Fundorte in Westasien und Nordafrika.
summary.en: Dung, goat bones and fat residues: how can we recognise early herding practices and the use of milk? Three findsites in Western Asia and North Africa.

labels.en: New Ways of Living After the Ice Age

description.de: Vom Ende der letzten Kaltzeit bis zu frühen bäuerlichen Gemeinschaften. Die Kapitel vergleichen Wohnen, Sammeln, Anbau und Tierhaltung in verschiedenen Regionen. Mesolithikum und Jungsteinzeit bezeichnen regionale Entwicklungen mit unterschiedlichen Zeitgrenzen.
description.en: From the end of the last glacial period to early farming communities. The chapters compare dwelling, foraging, cultivation and herding across regions. The Mesolithic and Neolithic describe regional developments with different time boundaries.

sourceRefs.locator: Paragraphs on lock steps and origin of construction cement, gravity and locomotives. Concluding paragraphs cover shovels 222 and 230 on 20 May 1913, locomotive 260 on 10 September, the Gatun tug on 26 September and Marmot’s December cut at Cucaracha.

Paragraphs on rail transport of spoil to Gatún Dam and the Naos–Flamenco breakwater, on extending the lake across the divide, and on the distinct modes of slope movement in the Culebra and Cucaracha slides.

Report of Electrical and Mechanical Engineer, pp. 115–116, “Up lockage of tug Gatun” and its return. Measured lift 64.7 feet. Pp. 118–119, first passage of the west chamber at Pedro Miguel by La Valley with Clapet No. 9 and barge No. 6, and trial at Gatún by the Ancon on 11 June.

Description of the canal, pp. 46–48, Gatun Lake, Gaillard Cut, Miraflores Lake and Locks. The bottom was 40 ft above sea level and the lake provided a channel 45 ft deep. P. 48 describes the paired chambers, three flights and the effect of Pacific tides on the lift at Miraflores.
Opening paragraphs on the 7 January 1914 completion of a staged crossing by the old French crane boat Alexandre La Valley and the inauguration with John A. Constantine serving as pilot aboard Ancon.

Tenth year, no. 2948, 16 August 1914, p. 1, col. 3 (digital file, pp. 2–3). Account of the special train and sailing from Cristóbal, lunch and steward Leddeke, Gamboa and dredge crews, spectators at Pedro Miguel, the outer buoys, transfer to boats and the anthem for President Porras.

Vol. VIII, no. 6, p. 52, letter dated 24 September 1914, opening paragraphs. The report distinguishes the 3 August Cristobal test to Balboa from the 15 August Ancon deep-water passage, then counts six vessels on 16 August.

The New Encyclopedic Atlas and Gazetteer of the World (1914), p. 66. Map of the route through Gatún Lake and the cut to the Pacific locks, with the railway, grid index, settlement names and coastal approaches.

Record Group 185, local identifier 185-G-0888, NAID 100996356. View from Cerro Luisa, 15 August 1914. Cropped archival photograph, file page with creator, identified location, date and public-domain status.

Announcement, 5 February 2016, paragraphs on the basins at Agua Clara and Cocolí and reuse of water from Gatún Lake per lockage.

labels.de: Mit der Ancon über die Wasserscheide
labels.en: Across the continental divide aboard Ancon

labels.de: 10. September 1913 · Der letzte Zug mit trocken gebaggertem Gestein
labels.en: 10 September 1913 · The last trainload of rock dug out on dry ground

summary.de: Lokomotive 260 zog die letzte auf trockenem Grund gebaggerte Fuhre aus dem Culebra-Einschnitt. Nach der Flutung gewannen Schwimmbagger die Fahrrinne zurück. Der Punkt bezeichnet den Einschnitt.
summary.en: Locomotive 260 hauled the last rock dug on dry ground from Culebra Cut. After flooding, floating dredges cleared the channel. The point identifies the cut.

labels.de: 26. September 1913 · Der Schlepper Gatun fährt durch drei Stufen
labels.en: 26 September 1913 · The tug Gatun ascends three steps

summary.de: Der Schlepper stieg bei der ersten Probeschleusung knapp zwanzig Meter. Am nächsten Morgen kehrte er durch dieselben Kammern zur Atlantikseite zurück.
summary.en: The working tug climbed nearly twenty metres in the first trial through the locks. Next morning it came down through the same flight to the Atlantic side.

labels.de: 7. Januar 1914 · Ein Kranschiff erreicht den Pazifik
labels.en: 7 January 1914 · A crane boat reaches the Pacific

summary.de: Die französische Alexandre La Valley, zuvor von der Atlantikseite heraufgekommen, fuhr durch die Pazifikschleusen. Damit hatte das Arbeitsschiff die Landenge in Etappen durchquert.
summary.en: The French crane boat Alexandre La Valley, previously brought up from the Atlantic side, passed through the Pacific locks, completing a crossing in stages.

labels.de: 15. August 1914 · Die Ancon auf der offiziellen Eröffnungsfahrt
labels.en: 15 August 1914 · Ancon on the official opening passage

summary.de: Der Lotse John A. Constantine führte den Dampfer von Cristóbal bis zu den äußeren pazifischen Fahrwassertonnen. Eine Aufnahme vom Cerro Luisa zeigt das Einlaufen in Pedro Miguel.
summary.en: The pilot John A. Constantine took the steamer from Cristóbal to the outer Pacific buoys. A photograph from Cerro Luisa shows it entering Pedro Miguel Locks.

labels.de: 18. September 1915 bis 15. April 1916 · Die Hänge schließen die Fahrrinne
labels.en: 18 September 1915 to 15 April 1916 · The banks close over the channel

summary.de: Die Hänge von Culebra schoben Material von beiden Seiten in die Fahrrinne. Rund vierzig Schiffe mussten über Gatún zum Atlantik zurück. Im April 1916 begann der reguläre Verkehr erneut.
summary.en: Moving slopes at Culebra sent material into the channel from both sides. Roughly forty vessels had to return through Gatún to the Atlantic. General traffic resumed in April 1916.

summary.de: Ein Schlepper steigt zum noch ansteigenden Gatúnsee auf, ein Kranschiff findet den Weg zum Pazifik. An Bord der Ancon erleben Gäste die erste offizielle Durchfahrt. Ein Jahr später schicken abrutschende Hänge die Schiffe zurück.
summary.en: A tug climbs to the still-rising Gatún Lake. A crane boat reaches the Pacific. Passengers aboard Ancon witness the official opening. A year later the movement of the hills sends ships back the way they came.

sourceRefs.locator: II.43 and III.1. Clovis dies at Paris and is buried in the church of the Holy Apostles that he and Clotild had built. The four sons are named and their inheritance described as equal. III.1 gives no meeting place or list of seats.

III.11. Chlothar and Childebert besiege Augustodunum. Godomar flees. Gregory links the siege with the acquisition of Burgundy.
IV.20–21. Childebert’s sickness and burial at Paris, Chlothar’s acquisition of the kingdom and treasure and his later burial by his four sons at Soissons.
IV.22, MGH SS rer. Merov. 1.1, pp. 154–155. Chilperic uses royal treasure and enters Paris. His brothers dislodge him. The narrative pairs each of the four kings with a predecessor and a sedes.
Abstract. Questions the degree to which Gregory’s pairing of 511 and 561 reflects formal settlements. His narrative served the political arguments of a later generation.

pp. 223–225, 237–239 and nn. 64–67. Shares in cities and aristocratic loyalty in the Treaty of Andelot. Gregory’s use of Burgundy and Austrasia, absence of Neustria in his work, and the emergence of the three regional kingdoms.

summary.de: Priskos kam durch Naissus. In der Nähe übergab ein römischer Befehlshaber der Gesandtschaft fünf Männer. Der Punkt markiert die Stadt. Attilas spätere Residenz ist räumlich ungewiss.
summary.en: Priscus passed through Naissus. Nearby a Roman commander handed five men to his embassy. The map locates the town. The residence reached later in the journey cannot be securely placed.

summary.de: 615 trat der zwölfjährige Pakal in Palenque die Herrschaft an. Eine Tafel im Palast zeigt seine Mutter Sak K’uk’ bei der Übergabe des Kopfschmucks.
summary.en: Twelve-year-old Pakal acceded at Palenque in 615. In the palace, a tablet portrays his mother Sak K’uk’ offering him the royal headdress.

labels.de: 794 · Wie viel Brot für einen Denar?
labels.en: 794 · How much bread for one denarius?

summary.de: In Frankfurt erließ die Versammlung Regeln für Getreide und Brot. Die Zahlen geben die Vorschrift wieder. Einen tatsächlichen Einkauf überliefern sie uns nicht.
summary.en: The assembly at Frankfurt set rates for grain and bread. These figures come from the ordinance. An individual purchase would require further evidence.

summary.de: Der Baum für die Maststütze wurde im Mai oder Juni 1042 gefällt. Das Schiff wurde damals oder bald darauf in Ostirland gebaut, wahrscheinlich im Raum Dublin. Die Karte zeigt die Region der vermuteten Werft.
summary.en: The oak for the keelson was felled in May or June 1042. The ship was built then or soon afterwards in eastern Ireland, probably around Dublin. The map locates the likely region of the yard.

labels.en: 1323 · A trading ship between three coasts

summary.de: Qingyuan ist der wahrscheinliche Ausgangshafen. Das Wrack liegt bei Sinan. Die Tempelgemeinschaft in Kyoto ist als Empfänger auf einem Etikett bezeugt.
summary.en: Qingyuan was the likely port of departure. The wreck lies off Sinan. A cargo tag names a temple community at Kyoto as a recipient.

labels.de: 1453 · Die bisherige Kathedrale wird zur Moschee
labels.en: 1453 · The former cathedral becomes a mosque

summary.de: 1453 ließ Mehmed II. die Hagia Sophia als Moschee einrichten. Der Bau der alten Kathedrale blieb an seinem Platz.
summary.en: In 1453 Mehmed II had Hagia Sophia converted into a mosque. The fabric of the old cathedral remained in place.

labels.de: 1519 · Moteuczoma II. und Cortés am südlichen Zugang
labels.en: 1519 · Moteuczoma II and Cortés on the southern approach

summary.de: Zwei Berichte über die Begegnung führen an den südlichen Zugang zur Inselstadt. Der Punkt bezeichnet die Gegend des Damms.
summary.en: Two accounts of the encounter lead to the southern approach to the island city. The point marks the general area of the causeway.

summary.de: Was verraten ein Schiffsbalken, ein Brotpreis und ein Frachtetikett über die Menschen, die sie hinterließen? Sieben Stationen führen vom spätantiken Balkan bis nach Tenochtitlan.
summary.en: What can a ship timber, a bread price and a cargo tag tell us about the people who left them? Seven stops lead from the late antique Balkans to Tenochtitlan.

description.de: Die Kapitel zur Völkerwanderung führen durch die spätrömische Welt. Die Funde an der unteren Weichsel reichen in die römische Kaiserzeit zurück und gehören zur Vorgeschichte der Reihe.
description.en: These chapters follow the Migration Period in the late Roman world. Evidence on the lower Vistula goes back to the Roman Imperial period and introduces the earlier history of the series.

sourceRefs.locator: Histories II.9, Merovech, Childeric and the tradition about Chlodio; II.37–38, the fighting near Poitiers and honours at Tours; III.1 and IV.22, the divisions and royal seats.

Notice pddn_hagio.202110061928562430200, Mort and Éléments d’identification: Radegund died at Poitiers in August 587.

Gregory IX.42; Epistolae 914, first paragraphs and final appeal: Chlothar’s resources, Agnes’s election, obedience of the founder, protection of property, and burial in the church dedicated to Mary even if unfinished.

No. 9, p. 22, c. 12, and p. 23, final subscription and dating clause. Judges from other provinces or regions, restitution from their own goods, and Paris as the place of issue.

pp. 227–231, figs. 5, 6 and 9, n. 12. Waterlogged graves at the eastern farm, winter 703/704 felling date for freshly worked oak of grave 27, and the excavator’s dating of the burial to early 704.
