No. 2921, Paris AN K 4 no. 7: original parchment; opening line names Pippin and Attigny, the following pleading names Fulrad, Ragana and her representative, the conclusion dates by Childeric.

Heading, opening and dating clause: 1 March 752, Verberie, rex Francorum. Narrative: Loba’s testament, Gislemar’s admission and surrender per festucam, Fulrad, and the preceding hearing before King Chilperic.
“The Carolingians”, opening paragraphs and notes 35–37, 46: late testimony about 751, Boniface, and papal letters recalling the anointing of Pippin and his sons in 754.

labels.en: The Merovingians and the Frankish kingdoms

summary.de: Das Grab wird gewöhnlich um 481/482 angesetzt. Der Stich von 1655 überliefert das Bild des verlorenen Originals.
summary.en: The burial is usually dated to around 481/482. A print published in 1655 preserves the design of the lost original.

summary.de: Die beiden Heere sind in derselben Gegend bezeugt. Beide Lesepfade öffnen die Schlacht bei Poitiers im selben Jahr.
summary.en: Both armies are attested in the same area. Both reading paths open the battle near Poitiers in the same year.

summary.de: Im Sommer tagten Bischöfe in Orléans. Nach Chlodwigs Tod traten seine Söhne die Nachfolge an.
summary.en: Bishops met at Orléans that summer. After Clovis died, his sons succeeded him.

summary.de: Paris, Orléans, Reims und Soissons dienen Gregor als Bezugspunkte für die Anteile von vier Brüdern.
summary.en: Gregory names Paris, Orléans, Reims and Soissons as seats of the four brothers.

summary.de: Im August wurde Radegunde bestattet. Im November kam der Vertrag von Andelot zustande. Cahors stand im Vertrag.
summary.en: Radegund was buried in August. The treaty followed at Andelot in November. Cahors was named in its clauses.

summary.de: Chlothar II. ließ nach der Vereinigung der Teilreiche in Paris ein Edikt ergehen.
summary.en: Following the reunion of the kingdoms, Chlothar II issued an edict at Paris.

labels.en: 625 · A plot of land and a coin

summary.de: Die Schenkung betrifft Paris. Die Münze mit dem Namen Madelinus wird um 625 nach Maastricht datiert.
summary.en: The donated property lay in Paris. A Maastricht coin bearing the name Madelinus is dated to around 625.

summary.de: Die Urkunde stammt aus Clichy. Der König nennt Saint-Denis als Ruhestätte seiner Eltern.
summary.en: The charter was issued at Clichy. The king identifies Saint-Denis as the place where his parents were buried.

summary.de: Das Eichenholz der Grabkammer wurde im Winter 703/704 gefällt. Das umgearbeitete Bett gehört zu ihrer Ausstattung.
summary.en: The chamber oak was felled in the winter of 703/704. The converted bed was placed inside the chamber.

labels.de: 751 · Wer ist im Juni der König?

summary.de: Die Attigny-Urkunde datiert nach Childerich III. Den Ort der Königserhebung Pippins überliefert eine spätere Erzählung.
summary.en: The Attigny charter dates by Childeric III. A later account supplies the location for Pippin’s elevation.

summary.de: Ein zweites Urteil für Abt Fulrad nennt Pippin im März 752 König der Franken.
summary.en: Another judgment for Abbot Fulrad calls Pippin king of the Franks in March 752.

summary.de: Papst Stephan II. salbte Pippin und seine Söhne. Der Bildvergleich im Kapitel stammt aus dem 13. Jahrhundert.
summary.en: Pope Stephen II anointed Pippin and his sons. The picture discussed in the chapter dates from the thirteenth century.

summary.de: Von Childerichs Siegelring bis zu Pippins Salbung. Zwölf Kartenstationen verbinden Königsfamilien, Münzmeister, Nonnen und Dorfbewohner. In Vouillé und in Poitiers lässt sich mitten im Geschehen das Kapitel wechseln.
summary.en: From Childeric’s signet to Pippin’s anointing. Twelve map stations connect royal families, moneyers, nuns and villagers. At Vouillé and Poitiers you can change chapters in the middle of the story.

sourceRefs.locator: Sections ‘Völker, Stämme, Volksstämme’ and ‘Wanderungen’ on the conventional 375–568 frame, changing groups and negotiations with the empire.
pp. 192–195. Jordanes, Getica 4.25–29, sixth-century setting, possible oral elements and the limits of the Scandinavian origin narrative.
pp. 228–230. Accounts of the lower Vistula in Roman-period sources and in Jordanes.
Olbia R-23 assemblage and fig. 19. Regional ceramic traditions and imported wares in the excavated contexts.
31.4.1–13. The two embassies, imperial recruitment hopes, boats, river conditions and food shortages.
Entry ‘Alaric’, opening extract. The formation of Alaric’s following and the sack of Rome in 410.
Hydatius under 409 and 411 for Hispania. Prosper under 439 and 442 for Carthage and the settlement.
Act XIII, pp. 259–261, lines 1–6 and 29–38. Regnal date, crops, names of the sellers and their marks.
p. 532, introduction and notes 4–8, on Wulfila at Constantinople in 360.
Pars posterior 65–71, reception at Rome, the senate, public expenses and the water supply of Ravenna.
Sections The four gospels in the Gothic language and Materials. Fourth-century translation, probable Ravenna production in the early sixth century, purple parchment, silver and gold inks.
Docs. 35–36, pp. 278–279. Copy preserved in a tenth-century manuscript, subscriptions of King Reccared and Queen Baddo at Toledo in 589.

labels.de: Die Völkerwanderung auf der Karte lesen
labels.en: Reading the Migration Period on the Map

summary.de: Antike Autoren und ein Gräberfeld geben unterschiedliche Hinweise auf Menschen im heutigen Nordpolen.
summary.en: Ancient writers and a cemetery offer different kinds of evidence for people in what is now northern Poland.

summary.de: In der weiteren Region finden Archäologen ähnliche Keramik. Zwischen einzelnen Werkstätten und einem politischen Verband liegen mehrere Deutungsschritte.
summary.en: Archaeologists find related ceramics across this region. Evidence for individual workshops and for a political community calls for different kinds of interpretation.

summary.de: Das Konzil von 360 verbindet den Bischof mit der kaiserlichen Hauptstadt.
summary.en: The council of 360 places the bishop in the imperial capital.

summary.de: Auf der anderen Seite der unteren Donau lag römisches Gebiet. Ammianus schildert die Aufnahme einer Gruppe und die Zurückweisung einer zweiten.
summary.en: Roman territory lay across the lower Danube. Ammianus describes one group gaining admission and another being turned away.

summary.de: In Rom lässt sich ein einzelner Schauplatz benennen. Für vandalische Gruppen auf der Iberischen Halbinsel bleibt die Ortsangabe viel gröber.
summary.en: At Rome the evidence names a specific city. The location recorded for Vandal groups in the Iberian Peninsula is much broader.

summary.de: In der römischen Hafenstadt wechselte die Herrschaft. Erst für spätere Jahre wird hier ein größerer politischer Raum gezeigt.
summary.en: Rule changed in the Roman port. The map shows a larger political territory for later years.

summary.de: Etwa fünfzig Jahre nach der Einnahme Karthagos verkauft ein Paar Nutzungsrechte. Die Holztafel trägt eine Datierung nach dem Regierungsjahr eines vandalischen Königs.
summary.en: Around fifty years after the capture of Carthage, a couple sells cultivation rights. The wooden record dates the transaction by a Vandal king’s regnal year.

summary.de: Der Senat und Papst Symmachus empfingen den König in Rom. Seine Residenz blieb in Ravenna.
summary.en: The Senate and Pope Symmachus received the king in Rome. His residence remained at Ravenna.

summary.de: Gregor nennt den zehnten Meilenstein von Poitiers. Die Lage des Schlachtfelds ist umstritten.
summary.en: Gregory mentions the tenth milestone from Poitiers. The precise battlefield is disputed.

summary.de: Während in Recópolis Glas verarbeitet wurde, traten die Bischöfe flussabwärts in Toledo zusammen.
summary.en: While glass was being worked at Reccopolis, the bishops gathered downstream at Toledo.

summary.de: Wo lassen sich Goten und ihre Nachbarn zu einem bestimmten Zeitpunkt tatsächlich fassen? Zehn Kartenstationen führen von den Gräbern an der Weichsel über den Schwarzmeerraum und die Donau bis zu den Höfen von Ravenna und Toledo. Für 410 sind Rom und Hispania zugleich zu sehen.
summary.en: Where can we place Goths and their neighbours at a particular moment? Ten map stops lead from cemeteries on the Vistula through the Black Sea region and across the Danube to the courts of Ravenna and Toledo. In 410 Rome and Hispania can be seen side by side.

description.de: Die Kapitel zur Völkerwanderung führen durch die spätrömische Welt. Die Funde an der unteren Weichsel reichen in die römische Kaiserzeit zurück und gehören zur Vorgeschichte der Reihe.
description.en: These chapters follow the Migration Period in the late Roman world. Evidence on the lower Vistula goes back to the Roman Imperial period and introduces the earlier history of the series.

sourceRefs.locator: Anales del Museo de América XX, pp. 264–267, ports, the foundation of San Felipe de Portobelo, the fairs, merchandise and provisioning. Pp. 267–269, especially p. 268, the two itineraries, the municipal warehouse built at Cruces in 1536, 47 compartments, enslaved households, river transport and cargo craft.

Section 2, “Description and history”, opening discussion of the itineraries. Follow the sequence Nombre de Dios, coastal navigation, Chagres, Venta de Cruces and Panamá Viejo. The evaluation dates the village of Cruces to 1533, before the warehouse. Also the 1597 transfer and the relocation of Panamá in 1673.

Printed p. 186, archaeological sites inventory, “Venta de Cruces”, period Colonial. The WGS 84 UTM reference 17 P 644522 1009307 converts to 9.12836 N, 79.68478 W. It locates the settlement rather than the warehouse footprint.

“Textual description of the boundary of the nominated property”, components 002 and 003, Camino de Cruces sections 1 and 2. Section 2 begins at Venta de Cruces near the northern entrance to the Culebra Cut. Compare proposed site maps 04 and 05 and the distinct archaeological-site point for Panamá Viejo in the opening table.

“Inversión extranjera y la construcción de la línea férrea”, passages on Manzanillo Island, the two port names, construction begun in 1850, 47.5 miles, the inauguration on 28 January 1855 and class fares. Later discussion of the French purchase of over 98% of railroad shares. DOI 10.18232/alhe.v22i2.588.
Chapter 2, “Migration to Panama in the 19th Century”, pp. 55–58. Origins of the railroad workforce and arrival of workers from China during construction.
“Panama Railroad at the Summit, 1855”, on the last rail laid 27 January and Robert Tomes’s account of buying oranges in the first year. Also “Barbacoas Bridge” and view of Front Street in Colón.

Smithsonian Libraries and Archives, BHL item 238774, single foldout map, compiled from the original surveys, 1857. Compare the Chagres, the railway alignment, and the track profile along the left edge. Item-level Copyright & Usage identifies the work as public domain; DOI 10.5962/bhl.title.140712.
TGN 7006458, coordinates 9.3500 N, 79.9000 W, Aspinwall as alternative name, historical note on the northern terminus. City-level point on Manzanillo Island.
List of events held in the Hôtel de la Société. Entry for the interoceanic canal congress, 15–29 May 1879. The institution gives its address as 184 boulevard Saint-Germain, Paris.
Catalogue record for the 68-page Paris printing with folded plates. The title identifies the technical report and fixes the day of the closing session.

France, instruction of 25 April designating Daniel Ammen and civil engineer Menocal. The paragraph defining the non-official character of the congress limits their participation to discussion by experts.

International congress and its vote (Menocal, Lépinay and Pedro Sosa). The passages on Dingler, Boyer and Bunau-Varilla describe transport of spoil, earth slides, Jamaican labour and the July 1886 Culebra contract. “Gustave Eiffel” dates the 1887 report, 1888 construction under the amended plan and stoppage.
Chapter on the Panama route, pp. 81–83, especially the ground at the divide, relation of the Chagres to the route, temporary lock design, court judgment, liquidator’s powers and cessation on 15 May.

29 November 2021, “Antecedentes históricos” and “Antes de la segunda guerra mundial”: September 1882 opening, choice of the slope of Cerro Ancón to catch breezes away from city wastewater, US acquisition and reuse of the grounds. MINSA gives 12 September for the opening. The thanksgiving Mass is separately dated to the 17th by Escobar. The station therefore identifies the opening by month.

Chapter VI, “Hospitales en la Época del Canal Francés”, pp. CXLIX–CLI. Companyo, his earlier work at Suez, Huerta de Gallo, the fundraising committee, the September thanksgiving Mass, transfers of patients, the sisters, Colón, the former Taboga hotel and the orphanage. Chapter VII, pp. CLXXIV–CLXXVI, reports the 1916 request for larger premises and lottery funding. Pp. CLXXXII–CLXXXIII name the four nursing graduates of 1912. For the 1924 opening date use the contemporary decrees, which supersede the December date printed on p. CLXXV.

Public Health Reports 19 (8), 19 February 1904, printed p. 277, “Hospitals”: wooden, separated pavilions of the French hospital, nursing by Sisters of Charity, twenty-four patients in the foreign section and twenty in the canal section. This is a count made before the US canal administration assumed the hospital.

“Gustave Eiffel”, final paragraphs on the first canal company, receivership and the appointment of a liquidator. Escobar, pp. CL–CLI, traces how the breakdown of the construction enterprise affected its hospitals.

Ficha P1405, Antiguo Hospital Gorgas, Calle Gorgas y Calle Juan de Arco Galindo, Ancón, records 659775.38 E, 990772.36 N in WGS84 / UTM zone 17N, converted to 8.96024° N, 79.54667° W. Marks the hospital complex as rebuilt from 1915 to 1919. For the continuity of the French hospital site see Escobar, p. CXLIX, and MINSA. Individual wards and earlier pavilions are not fixed by this point.

Chapter XVI, “Malaria Work and the Hospital System”, printed p. 226, paragraph beginning “The nursing force was composed”. Gorgas describes the Black maids and orderlies who worked in the French hospital, including direct care and manual work under the sisters’ supervision.

New West Indian Guide 59 (1–2), pp. 1–26. On pp. 8–10 Richardson cites Karner's letter in the Barbados Advocate, 23 January 1905, and the 1909 Weekly Illustrated Paper retrospective on recruitment by returnees. Bridgetown wharf, lighters, Carlisle Bay and the distinction between contracted and noncontract migrants appear on pp. 9–10.

Workforce recruitment, from the paragraph beginning ‘It was recognized early on’ through the separate discussions of Barbados and Jamaica. The figure of 19,900 is recruitment in Barbados. Jamaica refused recruiting and required intending emigrants to cover tax and passage. Skilled workers were among those able to pay.

Property 1376, Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison, N 13°05′48″ W 59°36′50″ and the accompanying property map. Locator for the historic town and its harbour rather than an individual 1905 boarding place.

The Canal Record, vol. V, no. 15, 6 December 1911, pp. 120–121. First column on the expected removal of the railway and dwellings already being taken down. The entries for Gatun, Bohio and Frijoles list the produce trade, housing, school and shops, 1908 counts and the burial of old Gatun under the dam. The editorial assessment of the losses occurs on p. 120.

La Prensa, 6 July 2014. The paragraphs beginning “A diferencia de lo que se cree comúnmente” and “Además, los trabajos del Canal” distinguish flooded Gorgona, the first relocation of Gatún and the later clearance of dry settlements. The preceding paragraphs reconstruct commerce and housing from tax records.

Cuadernos Nacionales 37, pp. 151–154, section “Estación de Gatún.” Figures 32 and 36 locate the original and relocated railway station and relate the latter to the buildings and shoreline. Figure 33 and the text on pp. 152–153 describe the platform, ticket office, telegraph and baggage room.

Tenth year, no. 2948, 16 August 1914, p. 1, col. 3 (digital file, pp. 2–3). Account of the special train and sailing from Cristóbal, lunch and steward Leddeke, Gamboa and dredge crews, spectators at Pedro Miguel, the outer buoys, transfer to boats and the anthem for President Porras.

Vol. VIII, no. 6, p. 52, letter dated 24 September 1914, opening paragraphs. The report distinguishes the 3 August Cristobal test to Balboa from the 15 August Ancon deep-water passage, then counts six vessels on 16 August.

Record Group 185, local identifier 185-G-0888, NAID 100996356. View from Cerro Luisa, 15 August 1914. Cropped archival photograph, file page with creator, identified location, date and public-domain status.
Opening paragraphs on the 7 January 1914 completion of a staged crossing by the old French crane boat Alexandre La Valley and the inauguration with John A. Constantine serving as pilot aboard Ancon.

Report of Electrical and Mechanical Engineer, pp. 115–116, “Up lockage of tug Gatun” and its return. Measured lift 64.7 feet. Pp. 118–119, first passage of the west chamber at Pedro Miguel by La Valley with Clapet No. 9 and barge No. 6, and trial at Gatún by the Ancon on 11 June.

Paragraphs on lock steps and origin of construction cement, gravity and locomotives. Concluding paragraphs cover shovels 222 and 230 on 20 May 1913, locomotive 260 on 10 September, the Gatun tug on 26 September and Marmot’s December cut at Cucaracha.

The New Encyclopedic Atlas and Gazetteer of the World (1914), p. 66. Map of the route through Gatún Lake and the cut to the Pacific locks, with the railway, grid index, settlement names and coastal approaches.
Gaceta Oficial núm. 18451, 1 November 1977. Entry names the two instruments and the agreements implementing them, dates the signature, entry into force and noon termination of the canal treaty.

Selected Documents no. 6C (January 1978), printed pp. 3–5, Washington signing ceremony and English translation of Torrijos’s reservations. Panama Canal Treaty, pp. 41–50, Articles II.2, III.3, XI.1–2 and XIII on the deadline, appointments, jurisdiction and property. Neutrality Treaty, pp. 51–52, Articles I–V. The Letter of Submittal, p. 6, distinguishes the joint declaration of 3 April 1964 from the two presidents’ agreement announced on 24 September 1965 to replace the 1903 convention.

Articles I, II and IV establish permanent neutrality and peaceful transit on equal terms for vessels of all nations. Article V provides that Panama alone will operate the canal after the canal treaty expires.

Exhibition script, sections 4.4–4.5 on the ballot and debate under the military government, 5.1 on the end of the zone, 8.2 on training and constitutional change, and 8.3 on the two separate December ceremonies, participants and clock.
Opening three paragraphs. Identifies the flag site outside the Administration Building and distinguishes the anniversary ceremony of 2019 from the transfer at noon on 31 December 1999.
Opening paragraph of the statement dated 14 December 1999. Sets the international commemoration and Carter’s role apart from the transfer due on 31 December.
Coordinate statement for the listed Canal Administration Building in Ancón, monument PA-08-120. The building is mapped to orient the ceremony outside it.

Chairman’s message, opening paragraph on 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2024. Printed p. 22, Water Use, graph 1, 542 hm³ for drinking water, 17% of 3,124 hm³; p. 23, Rainfall, graph 2, watershed rainfall of 2,118 mm and historical average 2,660 mm; p. 24, Pilot Plan for Water Treatment, April 2024 reverse-osmosis pilot at Escobal for a projected 2,500 residents.

1 May 2024, opening four paragraphs, fig. 1 and Main findings. May–December 2023 rainfall near the Gatún catchment, lake levels, ship number and size restrictions, rising urban demand and leakage, influence of El Niño, differing station trends and insufficient evidence for attribution of observed drying to human-caused warming.

PDF p. 1, paragraph giving the lake reference point 09°10′31.7″ N, 79°54′06.4″ W, with cross-references to the national mapping institute. PDF pp. 3–5, fishery and tables 1–2, listing Escobal among the fishing communities. The fisheries figures cited there come from 2004.

20 October 2023. Image description, on Sentinel-1 radar observations and year-colour assignment, and the Credits and Licence fields for the 1,623 × 1,623 JPEG. Blue 2020, green 2021, red 2022, with ships on Gatún Lake and offshore. CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO is an explicit licence option.

AA00016037/00033, typescript pp. 1–3, scans image0096–image0098. Page 2 records 18 years as an artisan and 30 on deck, and his tally of 5,330 transits.

AA00016037/00001, scans image0003–image0004, ‘The Contest’ and ‘The Entries’, for the circular sent to fifteen newspapers, relief packages, posting deadline and anniversary. List of entrants on image0005 and image0007 includes Clarke and Simmons.

Modern American History 7 (1), pp. 127–130, especially pp. 127 and 130. The author identifies the 112 written testimonies in Box 25 of the Isthmian Historical Society collection at the Library of Congress and discusses how they were solicited and kept.

Printed pp. 107–108, Foreign Minister Solís on breaking relations. Pp. 109–112, Guevara Paz, “Relato objetivo de lo ocurrido en Balboa el jueves 9 de enero”, first published by La Estrella de Panamá, 14 January 1964. Includes Díaz, Gorgas Hospital, the delegation and the testimony attributed to Carranza.
Report of 9 January 2014. Identifies the Instituto Nacional flag, its custodians, movement to the Canal Museum in 2013, textile treatment in Spain and exhibition in the former Balboa school.
Paragraphs on the 1964 flag dispute, interruption and resumption of relations, and US Senate votes on the two treaties in 1978.
OpenStreetMap way 609527463, Centro de Capacitación Ascanio Arosemena. Building point for the former school identified in the ACP exhibition notice. The map does not place individual marchers.
FRUS, 1964–1968, volume XXXI, document 410, 3 April 1964, pp. 867–869. The presidents discuss restoring diplomatic relations, naming representatives and the absence of preconditions.
24 September 1965. Presidential statements issued in Washington and Panama City, especially point 1 of the joint statement on the replacement of the 1903 treaty.

22 October 2006. Ballot question, voting and turnout tables and project footnote. 705,284 yes, 201,105 no, 9,967 blank and 7,673 invalid; 924,029 ballots, 2,132,842 registered. The printed 76.3% uses all ballots. The yes/no subtotal of 906,389 gives 77.8% yes.

Title XV, Chapter 1, Article 325, first, third and fourth paragraphs. A proposal for a third set of locks requires executive and legislative approval, then a national referendum at least three months after legislative approval.

24 April 2006. Section 1, p. 3 and fig. 1, two existing lanes, new locks at both ends, channels and maximum lake level. Section 5.6, pp. 47–48, fig. 32 and note 78, gravity, three basins per chamber, 60% reuse within the new system and projected 7% less water per transit than the old locks. Section 7, p. 53, proposal using existing reservoirs.

Report RL30981, updated 16 November 2006, pp. CRS-15–16, “Canal Expansion Project”. Torrijos on revenue for social programmes and the Coordinadora Campesina Contra los Embalses on the risk of displacement. These are arguments put forward during the campaign.

Final communiqué, 26 June 2016, paragraph beginning “The inaugural transit began”. Records a completed passage from Agua Clara on the Atlantic to Cocolí on the Pacific by Cosco Shipping Panama, bound for Asia.

Spanish section, pp. 29–30, “Crónica de un día inolvidable”, arrivals by bus, crowd at noon, entry at about 3 p.m. and ship’s horn at Cocolí. P. 53, training and chartered Baroque. English section, p. 191, completed inauguration and more than 200 transits through September; p. 193, Baroque and Oceanus trials.

Morning dispatch, 26 June 2016. Opening paragraphs identify the vessel formerly named Andronikos, departure from Piraeus and the start at Agua Clara; the Pacific-side passage was still expected as this was written.

29 April 2016, paragraphs identifying the two participating lines and their ships Andronikos and Thalatta, the venue, the notary, Jorge Quijano, the drawing of the two names and the selected ship’s length and beam.

30 April 2016. Opening paragraphs describe the previous morning’s draw in the rotunda using the national lottery urn. Reporter names Margarita Azucena, notary Víctor Aldana Aparicio and administrator Jorge Quijano, and identifies both ships.
“Centro de Visitantes de Agua Clara – Gatún” and “Exhibición panorámica”. The public visitor site overlooks the Caribbean-side works near Colón.

National Archives Identifier 100997804, caption 311-A on the photograph. The dated print shows staff and workers at the pay car. The NARA/DPLA item record and US public-domain statement accompany the 1,761 × 1,443 pixel file.

Scribner’s Magazine 57 (4), April 1915, p. 396 (wage rolls and European labourers) and p. 404, photograph caption ‘Pay car at Culebra, January 12, 1908’: the carriage had counters and separate entrance and exit. This is an account by the former chief engineer and then governor.

AA00016037/00101, typescript pp. 1–3 (scan files image0029–image0031). Arrival by railway at San Pablo in 1908, coal and track work, father's referral, friends at Tabernilla, January 1910 move to the Gatún spillway, railway assignments and the concrete crane. The date and location of his first shift follow the first-person text.

Annex 4, Figure 1, between printed pp. 2 and 3. Overlay of the 1909 street plan labelled ‘Old town of Culebra’ on the March 1947 contours and slide limits. Approximate site on the west bank near Zion Hill. Neither the pay-car siding nor the precise 1906 office is identified on this map.

labels.de: 1536 · Die Stadt Panamá baut ein Lagerhaus in Cruces
labels.en: 1536 · Panamá builds a warehouse at Cruces

summary.de: Am Río Chagres wechselte die Ladung zwischen den Lastkähnen und den Maultieren. Das städtische Lagerhaus von 1536 hatte 47 Kammern.
summary.en: Cargo switched between river craft and pack mules on the Chagres. The municipal warehouse built here in 1536 had forty-seven compartments.

labels.de: 28. Januar 1855 · Der erste Zug durchquert die Landenge
labels.en: 28 January 1855 · The first train crosses the isthmus

summary.de: Am 28. Januar 1855 fuhr der Eröffnungszug von Colón, auch Aspinwall genannt, nach Panamá. Die Strecke maß rund 76 Kilometer.
summary.en: On 28 January 1855 the inaugural train ran from Colón, also called Aspinwall, to Panamá. The line was 47.5 miles long.

labels.de: 29. Mai 1879 · Die Mehrheit stimmt für einen Kanal auf Meereshöhe
labels.en: 29 May 1879 · A majority votes for a sea-level canal

summary.de: Der Pariser Kongress zieht einen Durchstich in Panama dem Plan für einen Schleusenkanal und einer Route durch Nicaragua vor. Der Ingenieur Pedro Sosa aus Panama gehört zu den Befürwortern.
summary.en: In Paris the majority favours a sea-level cut in Panama. Delegates have also heard a lock proposal for Panama and a route through Nicaragua. Pedro Sosa of Panama supports the cut.

labels.de: September 1882 · Die Schwestern am Cerro Ancón
labels.en: September 1882 · The sisters on Ancón Hill

summary.de: Die französische Kanalgesellschaft eröffnete auf dem Hang ihr Zentralkrankenhaus. Die Schwestern vom heiligen Vinzenz von Paul empfingen dort auch Kranke aus den Stationen entlang der Kanalbaustellen.
summary.en: The French canal company opened its central hospital on the hill. The Sisters of St Vincent de Paul received patients referred by dispensaries along the excavations.

labels.de: 23. Januar 1905 · Wer in Bridgetown an Bord ging

summary.de: William J. Karner wirbt im Barbados Advocate um Arbeitskräfte für die Kanalbaukommission. Später erzählen Rückkehrer in den Dörfern von ihren Erfahrungen, und am Kai von Bridgetown verabschieden Familien die nächsten Reisenden.
summary.en: William J. Karner appeals for canal recruits in the Barbados Advocate. Men returning to the island share their experiences, and families gather at the Bridgetown wharf to see off those who follow.

labels.de: 1908 · Gatún räumt den Platz für den Damm
labels.en: 1908 · Gatún moves from the dam site

summary.de: Das Dorf am Fluss ist 1908 aufgegeben. Die meisten Gebäude stehen danach wieder in Nuevo Gatún. Fels und Erde des Damms bedecken den früheren Standort.
summary.en: The riverside village has been abandoned by 1908. Most of its buildings are re-erected at Nuevo Gatún. Earth and rock for the dam cover the old site.

labels.de: 15. August 1914 · Die Ancon auf der offiziellen Eröffnungsfahrt
labels.en: 15 August 1914 · Ancon on the official opening passage

summary.de: Der Lotse John A. Constantine führte den Dampfer von Cristóbal bis zu den äußeren pazifischen Fahrwassertonnen. Eine Aufnahme vom Cerro Luisa zeigt das Einlaufen in Pedro Miguel.
summary.en: The pilot John A. Constantine took the steamer from Cristóbal to the outer Pacific buoys. A photograph from Cerro Luisa shows it entering Pedro Miguel Locks.

labels.de: 31. Dezember 1999, 12 Uhr Ortszeit · Zwei Feiern und ein genauer Zeitpunkt
labels.en: 31 December 1999, noon Panama time · Two ceremonies and an hour set by treaty

summary.de: Vor dem Verwaltungsgebäude in Balboa zählt eine Uhr die Zeit bis zur Übergabe. Um zwölf Uhr mittags übernimmt Panama den Betrieb. Die internationale Feier in Miraflores lag bereits siebzehn Tage zurück.
summary.en: A clock outside the Administration Building in Balboa counts down to the handover. Panama takes over at noon, seventeen days after the international ceremony at Miraflores.

labels.de: 1. Oktober 2023 bis 30. September 2024 · Wenig Regen im Einzugsgebiet des Kanals
labels.en: 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2024 · A rain shortage in the canal watershed

summary.de: Für das Geschäftsjahr 2023/24 verzeichnet die Kanalbehörde 2.118 Millimeter Regen im Einzugsgebiet und 542 Millionen Kubikmeter für Trinkwasser. Der Punkt bezeichnet den Gatúnsee. Die ESA-Aufnahmen stammen aus den Jahren vor der trockenen Regenzeit.
summary.en: For fiscal year 2023/24 the authority records 2,118 millimetres of rain across the watershed and 542 million cubic metres for drinking water. The point represents Gatún Lake. The ESA imagery predates the dry rainy season.

summary.de: Ein Magazin am Chagres, ein Lohnwagen und die Fahrt der Ancon erzählen, wer die Landenge überquerte und wer ihre Wasserwege schuf. Vom alten Gatún führt der Weg bis zur Übergabe an Panama und zur Dürre von 2023.
summary.en: A Chagres warehouse, a pay car and the voyage of the Ancon reveal who crossed the isthmus and who made its waterways. From old Gatún the guide follows the handover to Panama and the drought of 2023.

description.de: 1801–1900. Ein kalendarischer Zeitbereich; regionale Epochen können ihn unterschiedlich gliedern.
description.en: 1801–1900. A calendar grouping; regional periods may divide it differently.

sourceRefs.locator: In The Fortified Viking Age, pp. 78–80, fig. 5 and tables 1–2. Riverbank lane before 720, plots 6–8 m wide, Rhineland barrels reused in wells, sequence of individual coin finds and the predominance of Series X from about 725.

European Journal of Archaeology 18, pp. 497–523. The reassessment of the 1985–86 excavations at Sct Nicolajgade 8 uses domestic activity and building remains to propose early permanent occupation on part of the market site.

Archaeological and Anthropological Sciences 14, article 180. Site and materials, table 1 and figs. 1b, 7–8. ASR 9 Post Office site (55°19′44.7″N, 8°46′08.7″E). Early workshop c. 700–720, later workshop c. 760–790. White from bubbles in remelted gold-leaf backing glass and evidence for adding colourants on site.

Chapters X–XI. Witmar as a witness, loss of the books en route, permission to preach, captive Christians, Herigar and his church. The narrative is used for the visit. Modern site identification follows the Swedish History Museum.
Opening paragraphs. Rimbert wrote about 865–875. The museum dates Ansgar and Witmar’s first journey to 830 and distinguishes it from Ansgar’s later visit.
Handelsplatsen Birka. Björkö stood at a Baltic inlet at the time of the trading settlement. The present lake resulted from land uplift. Also explains the deposits called Svarta jorden.
Geographical data, component 555-001, Birka on Björkö (not 555-002, Hovgården). A rounded site point is shared by the harbour, burial and hoard stations.
Collegium Medievale 29, pp. 84–87, “Oseberggravningen”; fig. 2 and pp. 84–85 on five bark-edge samples, the two posts and ridge, the pressure-deformed chamber, and drawings by Glende and Beck.

“What do the motifs on the Oseberg tapestry signify?”, “Exotic goods from Persia and Byzantium” and “The colours that disappeared”; clothing strips, the reversed silk, tools and Sofie Krafft’s 41 drawings of 110 silk pieces.
Project introduction and research areas 1–3. Over 80 figured fragments, visible motifs, faded dyes and questions about how the original scenes fitted together.
Opening account of the burial and the four sleighs, followed by “Carvings and ornamentation”. The museum distinguishes three richly carved sleighs and discusses their use before burial.
Hull and rowing holes, the ship built in 820, burial of two women in 834 and the uncertainty over their identities and status.

U841.4 and U842.2, two camps and continued presence; U870.6, four months at Ail Cluaithe; U871.2, Áth Cliath, the leaders, 200 ships and the three groups brought back as captives; U902.2 and U917.4, the defenders driven out and Sitriuc’s entry. U980.1 and U983.2, the battle of Tara and later coalitions.

EMAP Report 7.1, printed pp. 53–55, discussion of captive-taking, trade in enslaved people at Dublin, possibilities of domestic enslavement or onward sale, and the limits of the evidence for different destinations.
Section 2.1.1–2.1.2, printed pp. 3–4. The two placenames, proposed camp by the pool, events of 902 and 917 and changing focus around the Liffey shore at Fishamble Street and Wood Quay.
EMC 1065.0059, obverse and reverse. Entries for ruler, York mint, Raven / Small Cross type, moneyer Æthelferth, spelling on this specimen and weight of 1.17 g.

Rollason, historical sources, the capture in 866–867 and Northumbrian councillors; Blackburn, coinage under Olaf, fig. 82.2 and discussion of the Raven issue under the two Olafs. Craft synthesis, 16–22 Coppergate, pp. 476–481.

“The Jelling Stone”, translated inscription and photographs. The museum dates the raising to c. 965. Harald’s parents and claims about Denmark, Norway and Christianity, earlier Christian objects and Harald Klak’s baptism at Mainz in 826.

Antiquity 97, 1262–1278. Table 1, introduction on the north mound, “Ravnunge-Tue and the Jelling stones”, figures 9–10, “Sources of error” and conclusion. Læborg’s signed dedication and proposed attribution of Jelling 2, weathering at Jelling 1, variants of Thyra’s epithet, and limits of the proposed reburial. The authors give 959/60 for wood from the chamber.

Danish Journal of Archaeology 3(2), pp. 168–170, tables 1–2 and discussion immediately after table 2. Mid-tenth century up to c. 960 for Jelling 1. The chamber wood is reported as 958/59. Historical dating proposals for Jelling 2 differ.

Figures 2–6 and English summary under “Stone for his parents” and “Small silver cup”. Vertical and horizontal writing, reliefs, purple silk, and the 4.3 cm silver cup with gilding and entwined animals from the north mound.

Nature 601, pp. 388–391. Three worked pieces of wood, the metal-tool cuts and Norse depositional context, Table 1 and Fig. 2 on the radiocarbon signal and counting rings to the surviving outside edge. Published online in 2021.

“Discovery of the Site and Initial Excavations (1960–1968)”. Turf construction in eight buildings, bronze ring-headed pin in a cooking pit, stone lamp and spindle whorl in another building, ship nails and iron slag.
Collection entry “Bog Iron Nail, L’Anse aux Meadows, Newfoundland”. Slag and iron from the excavated nail support smelting of local bog ore. The four nails illustrated on that page are reproductions.
Appendix 1, pp. 30–31, manuscript witnesses AM 544 4to and GKS 1005 fol., and “B. Differences”: one planned expedition in Eiríks saga rauða and four in Grœnlendinga saga.

Introductory chronology, “Geographical areas of the Norse settlements and settlement pattern” and “Natural resources”. The written sources place one migration from Iceland to Southwest Greenland under Erik the Red around 985. The Western Settlement was in the Nuuk region; archaeological and radiocarbon evidence in the Eastern Settlement reaches at least the mid-fifteenth century.

Printed pp. 183–186, keelson sample D2-4 and its final spring ring; pp. 187–189, “Parallels in Irish and English ship-finds”, esp. fig. 55 (Fishamble Street stems T357/T364 and corresponding elements of Skuldelev 2) and text on parallels in Danish-built vessels.
Opening account, dating the build to around 1042 in the vicinity of Dublin through the oak tree rings.

Collection overview, paragraphs on wooden pathways and property boundaries, reused ship timbers in dock walls, drains and paths; the Fishamble Street amber worker’s floor with several hundred flakes and splinters.

Printed pp. 146, 148–149 and 152–153. P. 146 describes the transmitted attestations of 1409, 1414 and 1424. Document 49 gives the three Sunday banns, local and foreign witnesses, and the two clerics’ seals. Document 52 names the four men who attended in 1408 and attested in Iceland in 1414. Facsimile of the edition with facing original text and Danish translation.

“Kirkens vinduer” on the round arched east window and other flat lintels; “Brylluppet i Hvalseyfjordens kirke” on the September 1408 wedding, the document at Garðar in 1409 and the journey back to Iceland.
Collection item DMR-217737, ruin 1, group Ø83, NKAH 4427 (Hvalsey church). Location field 60.82883° N, 45.78261° W. Modern survey photograph dated 1935.

Section “Segmented metal foil beads”, pp. 161 and 165 and fig. 5a–c (e.g. ASR9x113 59). Manufacture, silver foil, amber-brown and colourless outer glass, joined segments and the visible structure of broken specimens. Opening section on the continued small-scale production in the ninth century.
Object 106842_HST, accession 34000, Bj 515. Find context, excavator, 1877, silver and glass. The 2021 exhibition label gives the proposed reading of the Arabic inscription.

Scanning 37, pp. 131–137. Materials, p. 132 and supplementary fig. S1, for burial layout, oval brooches, clothes, position and approximate date. Results and figs. 1–3 for filing marks and composition. Discussion accompanying fig. 4 for the favoured dedication and the conditional reading “God willing” if a missing stroke is supplied.
Media ID ba934209-835b-4b3c-ab7a-73126a4375a9, direct association with object 106842_HST, named photographer and CC BY 4.0 licence.
The Archaeology of York 17/5, table 11 and pp. 341–345, figs 140–142. Context, needle binding, shaping the heel, worn sole and outline of a probable patch.
SC1981-7_SF13517, catalogue 1309; coverage c. 930–975, madder at the ankle and no dye elsewhere.
The Archaeology of York 17/11, pp. 1787–1788, 1800–1803 and figs 843–844. A 4B pit, dyes and needles, including their concentration on Tenement C and a previously unused silk offcut.

The Archaeology of York 8/5. Abstract and Period 4B on the properties; Structure 5/1, pp. 622–624 and fig. 212; provisional building chronology p. 798. The report dates wall timbers to winter 961/62 and identifies reused wood at the entrance.
Monument MYO5075, Location: British National Grid SE 6044 5169. Converted to WGS84 and rounded for orientation.

“Gorm the Old authored Denmark’s name certificate” and “Two monuments from Danish history”. Gorm’s commissioning formula, the museum’s rendering of Thyra’s epithet, c. 950, and the photograph “The small Jelling stone” by Roberto Fortuna, CC BY-SA 2.0.

Abstract of chapter 12 in Jelling – Monuments and Landscape, pp. 313–332. The smaller stone is no longer in its original position. Excavation during protection works in 2011 re-examined the central area and the position of the larger stone.

SC1365, “Summary” and “Location”; twin summits, 1974–75 excavation, fifth trench on the eastern side, bedding trench, vitrified stone and three radiocarbon determinations in the sixth to ninth centuries. Site coordinates WGS84, 55.936756 N, 4.563298 W.
“Under siege”, identification of the 870 siege of the Rock, the Dublin leaders Olaf and Ivar, and forced removals following the four-month siege.

Chapter 7, pp. 102–108, Figs. 7.2–4 and Table 7.1. Hearth 4A76P west of the brook, 15 grey-green chert flakes one metre west of the fire, the nail one metre southeast. With 1950 as BP reference, the reported two-sigma charcoal ranges are AD 900–910 and 960–1040 for Beta-252632 and AD 990–1150 for Beta-252633. The map uses their outer envelope; occupation was episodic. pp. 115–116 and Tables 7.5–6 describe birds on the other, upper terrace.

Arctic Anthropology 49(1), pp. 68–87, DOI 10.1353/arc.2012.0015. Abstract and Table 1 discuss the site in relation to Beothuk ancestors, the charcoal determinations for hearth 4A76P2 and seasonal harvesting of birds.
First two paragraphs. Archaeological evidence of Indigenous use over six millennia and Dorset camps on the south shore more than two centuries before the Norse.

labels.de: frühes 8. Jahrhundert, vor 720 · Parzellen an einer Gasse
labels.en: early eighth century, before 720 · Plots beside a narrow lane

summary.de: Noch vor 720 lagen am Fluss schmale Parzellen beiderseits einer Gasse. Der Punkt liegt im ausgegrabenen Marktgebiet.
summary.en: By 720 narrow plots stood on either side of a lane by the river. The point marks the excavated market area.

labels.de: um 830 · Ansgar und Witmar erreichen den Hafen
labels.en: around 830 · Ansgar and Witmar reach the harbour

summary.de: Rimbert schildert die Ankunft der beiden Mönche, die Gefangenen und den Ortsvorsteher Hergeir. Der Punkt bezeichnet die Handelsstadt auf Björkö.
summary.en: Rimbert recounts the monks’ arrival and describes captives and the town’s reeve, Hergeir. The point marks the trading settlement on Björkö.

labels.de: 834 · Die Kammer und die Gewebe der beiden Frauen
labels.en: 834 · The chamber and the women’s textiles

summary.de: Das Holz der Kammer datiert die Bestattung in das Jahr 834. Gewebebänder, Seidenstreifen und Werkzeuge erschließen die Arbeit an Textilien, die bereits vor der Bestattung gebraucht wurden.
summary.en: The chamber timbers date the burial to 834. Woven bands, strips of silk and tools provide evidence of textile work and of the use of fabrics before burial.

summary.de: Die Annalen melden, dass Amlaíb und Ímar mit Gefangenen nach Áth Cliath kamen. Sie zählen Schiffe und nennen Gruppen von Verschleppten. Was aus den einzelnen Menschen wurde, steht dort nicht.
summary.en: The annals say that Amlaíb and Ímar brought captives to Áth Cliath. They count ships and name groups of people who were taken. Individual fates go unrecorded.

labels.de: 939–941, Regierungszeit · Der Rabenpenny des Münzers Æthelferth

summary.de: Unter Amlaíb mac Gofraid begann in York die Prägung der Rabenpennys. Einzelne Stücke könnten noch unter seinem Nachfolger entstanden sein. Die Karte zeigt die Münzstadt.
summary.en: York began issuing Raven pennies under Amlaíb mac Gofraid. Some specimens may belong to his successor. The map identifies the mint town.

labels.de: um 965 · Haralds Stein und die Hand des Runenmeisters
labels.en: around 965 · Harald’s stone and the carver’s hand

summary.de: Harald gedenkt seiner Eltern und beansprucht die Christianisierung der Dänen für sich. Die Rillen der Schrift legen nahe, dass Ravnunge-Tue die Runen schlug.
summary.en: Harald commemorates his parents and claims credit for the conversion of the Danes. The carved grooves suggest that Ravnunge-Tue cut the inscription.

summary.de: Die drei Hölzer datieren Arbeiten auf 1021. Nägel, Schlacke und Spinnwirtel bezeugen weitere Tätigkeiten im Lager, deren genaues Jahr offenbleibt.
summary.en: Three timbers date work at the camp to 1021. Nails, slag and a spindle whorl attest other activities there whose precise year is unknown.

labels.de: 1042 · Die Eiche für die Maststütze von Skuldelev 2
labels.en: 1042 · The oak for the keelson of Skuldelev 2

summary.de: Die Eiche für die Maststütze fiel im Mai oder Juni 1042. Der Bau des Langschiffs wird im Raum Dublin vermutet. Zwei in der Stadt ausgegrabene Stevenstücke zeigen vergleichbare Arbeit an anderen Schiffen.
summary.en: The oak for the keelson was felled in May or June 1042. The longship was probably built in the Dublin region. Two stem timbers excavated in the town show comparable work on other vessels.

labels.de: 1408 · Die Hochzeit von Sigríður und Þorsteinn

summary.de: Im September 1408 heirateten Sigríður Björnsdóttir und Þorsteinn Ólafsson in der Kirche von Hvalsey. Die Bestätigung der Geistlichen in Garðar und spätere Zeugenaussagen in Island betreffen dieselbe Ehe.
summary.en: In September 1408 Sigríður Björnsdóttir and Þorsteinn Ólafsson married in Hvalsey church. The Garðar clerics’ declaration and later testimony in Iceland concern the same marriage.

summary.de: Neun Stationen führen vom Markt am Fluss in Ribe über Gefangene in Dublin, eine Königsmünze und einen Runenstein bis zur nordischen Siedlung auf Neufundland. Ein Ausblick führt ins mittelalterliche Grönland.
summary.en: Nine stops lead from the riverside market in Ribe to captives in Dublin, a royal penny, a rune stone and Norse woodworking in Newfoundland. A final stop visits medieval Greenland.

sourceRefs.locator: Introduction, pp. 8–11, and editions, pp. 261–289. Tonyukuk I W 1–7, I S 1–5 and II E 4–8 for the counsellor’s narrative. KT S 1–13, E 1–5, N 9–13 and NE, SE for the court address, dates, mourners and work. BK E 2–24, S 10–15, N 9–10 and SW for shared text, funerary gifts, marriages and the second colophon.

Monument I, S 1–13, N 9–13, NE and SE, pp. 862–865, 870–871. The NE inscription separates the funeral from completion in the following animal year. The SE colophon records twenty days. Note 2, pp. 872–873, gives the reciprocal Türgesh marriages on monument II.
Dissertation, §2.5.2.1, “The entrance part (Trench 2, 8, 9)”, pp. 35–37, figs. 5–6. Plan of the eastern approach, photographs of the ram statues and fragments of roof tile and red plaster.

Appendix, printed pp. 212–216, particularly p. 214, paragraphs on the relationship with the Tang and on the qağan as an adopted son. The emperor extends that kinship language to Kül Tegin, the younger brother.

Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape Management Plan, §3.1.5, pp. 25–26, site coordinate table, row 1, “Turkish Memorials of Khöshöö Tsaidam”. The Kul tegin and Bilge Khan rows give 47°33′24.91″ N with 102°49′53.85″ E and 102°50′11.58″ E. The printed latitude and longitude column headings are transposed. A rounded midpoint orients the reader to the paired complexes.
Summary, author and licensing, original photograph of 15 July 2015, portrait display 3,648 × 5,472 pixels. CC BY-SA 4.0. The stone and its fracture are visible in the museum display.

Appendix A in Carole Hillenbrand, Turkish Myth and Muslim Symbol. Historia, ed. Pérez Martín, 113.5–123.16. Opening passage on the wagons, the army’s provisions and the townspeople’s request to keep their property in return for surrender.

Chapter 24, Armenian-era year 513, especially printed pp. 163–165 (Armenian pp. 134–136): two places of refuge, provisions, burial and usury. Chapter 25, pp. 167–171 (Armenian pp. 137–140): the names used for the two rulers, the captive’s release and his blinding.

Turkish Myth and Muslim Symbol, ch. 2, pp. 26–31, Arabic mirror for princes Sirāj al-mulūk by al-Turtushi, translation and commentary. Reversal of the captive and captor in a question in the literary dialogue. The account belongs to the early twelfth century.

“Malazgirt / Manazkert Citadel”, pp. 44–45, Location and Accessibility. The survey places the historic town’s citadel at 39.14692° N, 42.54504° E. This identifies the locality, whose walls also figure in Attaleiates, without assigning a location to the emperor’s capture.
Byzantinische Zeitschrift 105.2, pp. 834–835, n. 34. Conflicting reports arriving at the imperial camp, Attaleiates 125.15–126.10. DOI 10.1515/bz.2012.0033.

Introduction pp. 6–14, 23–25 on dates, manuscript and hands. Preface and dialects, pp. 70–85, especially p. 84 on settlements around Kashgar. Entries ötüš (game), adaš (close friend), idiš (drinking bowl, wider sense among the named groups) and uwuš (crumbs), p. 104. Āy (moon, month, summer verse and full-moon proverb), p. 119. Kändük (Känčäk flour container), p. 357. The map is inset between pp. 82 and 83.

TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi, vol. 9, pp. 446–449. Opening paragraphs on dates and readership. Sections 1–8, followed by paragraph on past-tense verb headwords. Map paragraph and omissions (Çigil, Suvar). Final paragraph, extent of 319 leaves.

Second edition. Imprint and pp. 19–21 for Millet Yazma Eser Kütüphanesi, Ali Emîrî Arabî 4189, court and dating. Eyewitness accounts pp. 21–32, especially Kilisli Rifat on broken binding, ordering and numbering the leaves pp. 30–31. Bibliography, entry for Kilisli’s first three-volume edition, Istanbul, 1333–1335 AH.

Dissertation, pp. 93–101. Dates and revisions, Cairo ownership note (CU 1), discussion on shared Kipchak and Turkmen forms in fifteen lines, attribution by handwriting, red rubrics and overwriting, vowel marks, colophon (CU 638, line 13) and alternatives Damascus or Cairo.
City record 98182, 33.34058 N, 44.40088 E. Approximate location of the city addressed, not a specified palace.
Kül Tegin monument, South 1–13 and the southeast colophon, pp. 862–865, 871. Bilge Qaghan addresses his listeners, and Yollug Tegin names his work at the memorial.
Inscriptions, individual entries for the north and west mosque portals, mihrab dome, west hospital portal, mosque minbar balustrade and central star. Includes Arabic terms and English renderings.

Description, passages on the north and west portals, pseudo-kündekari and openwork of the wooden minbar, and the three-iwan hospital with partial upper floor. How Monument was dated, two AH 626 inscriptions.

Printed pp. 87–90, “Documents for Dating the Building”. Transcribes and locates signatures, describes the twelve-pointed star and rail on the east face of the minbar, gives AH 638 and compares opinions on the 22-line mosque charter and the loss of the hospital deed.

Belleten 12/45. Pp. 55–58 on kitchen and staff, 63–67 on income and shops, 84 on the 10.64 m scroll and its two faces. Edition of the Arabic deed and addenda pp. 90–108, Turkish translation pp. 109–128, esp. pp. 113–115, lines 145–230, on pay, equipment and beneficiaries, and p. 117, lines 293–295, on the written deed in 645 AH.
Anatolian Studies 26, pp. 69–103, especially n. 32 on the two portals, the inscription of 638 AH, the disagreement over Karatay’s building role and the deed inscribed in 645 AH.

Karatay Hanı, paragraphs on the hall with rock-cut troughs and tethering holes, the two entrance inscriptions and the foundation’s provisions. Embedded map centres on the monument at 38.643978° N, 35.935351° E.

Khans Area monument inventory, entries ‘Orhan Ghazi Mosque’, ‘Orhan Turkish Bath (Mirrored Bazaar)’ and ‘Emir Khan’. The door inscription recalls foundation in 1339, burning in 1413 and repair in 1417. The inn generated revenue for the complex.

Bursa architectural inventory A106, Ayrıntılı Tanımı. Windowless storerooms below, inhabited rooms with a window and hearth above, counts of rooms and the rear stable. The inventory records later restoration.
Advisory body evaluation, Description of the property, component 1 (Orhan Ghazi complex, school, bath, kitchen and later town hall), components 2, 3, 5, 6 and 8, and History and development.
Bursa and Cumalıkızık property description. The village is identified as the waqf village belonging to the foundation of Orhan Ghazi.

In Remembering and Forgetting the Ancient City, chapter 7, pp. 167–169, figs 7.1–7.2. The walled hill, pre-Ottoman town, hot springs, east–west expansion, sites selected by Murad I and Bayezid I, and Bursa during the succession to Bayezid.
Egerton MS 2817, one item, 1453. The catalogue describes the Greek text, the sultan’s monogram and the Arabic-script date and vizier’s signature.

Opening section, translation from the Paris Ottoman Turkish text, envoys with the keys, property and enslaved people, annual tax, bells, new churches and customs. Discussion of Lomellino’s letter and flight by sea at notes 26–30. Reprinted in Essays in Ottoman History, pp. 275–376.
Tarih İncelemeleri Dergisi 36/2, pp. 601–604, especially notes 59–65. Compares Lomellino, Doukas and Barbaro, describes taxation and names Greek, Italian and Ottoman witnesses to the grant.

MA thesis, pp. 41–43 on the envoys, pp. 113–118 on the scope, dating and omissions of the survey. Sections 3.6.1–2, pp. 123–125, record Marya Maryana’s houses and oven, the brothers de Franchi, Fabyan and Anton di Laştergo. Note 760 identifies the Genoese notarial act for the smith.

Museum location and map for the watchtower of medieval Pera (approximately 41.02565 N, 28.97413 E). The tower is a landmark for the historic district on the north shore. The places where the charter was delivered, the letter written and individual households stood are not identified.
Introduction pp. 1–3, translation of the foundation conditions and map I.1 of the kitchen on the lane above al-Wad. Chapter 2, pp. 39–70, especially pp. 46–65 on revenues, employees and provisioning.

Journal of Interdisciplinary History 35.3, pp. 485–487 with note 8. The Jerusalem menu, the night before Friday, portions and the order in which the staff, residents and poor ate. DOI 10.1162/0022195052564252. Author’s accessible copy.
Inventory 2192. Description, provenance and colophon, AH 964. Fol. 1a for the tuğra, 9b–10a for the Jerusalem buildings, 12a–14b for expenditure, 49a for the founder’s seal and witnesses.

Cihannüma 12/1, p. 15, section on women acting as agents and n. 37: BOA, MŞH. ŞSC. d., Bursa 2458, A/3, fol. 345a, Jumada II 885 / August 1480. The property, neighbourhood, names, guardianship of two orphans and the form of sale.

VIII. Uluslararası Ahilik Sempozyumu, vol. II, pp. 172–173, nn. 22–23 (BŞS 4A, fol. 310, and 3A, fol. 174b): Fatma Hatun’s lease of the Doğangözü Han and Paşa Hatun’s dye-shop lease. P. 176, n. 42 (3A, fol. 345a): Nefise, Gülşah, Gülbahar and the names of the two wards.
TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi, vol. 6 (1992), pp. 20–22, especially p. 21, passage on bey‘ bi’l-istiğlâl: use, lease to the previous owner and redemption on repayment.
The history identifies the mosque as the district’s namesake; Hakkında and the map link give 40.18421 N, 29.0572042 E. Orientation in the quarter only, not the location of the house or court.

Galata survey, preamble and quarters Zani Drapora and Zani Dabdan, pp. 217–222. The register survives in fragments. The preamble specifies poll-tax liability, property confiscated for the treasury and rent. See Somer, pp. 114, 123–125, for the text and named entries.

labels.de: Von den Orchoninschriften zur osmanischen Stadt
labels.en: From the Orkhon inscriptions to the Ottoman city

labels.de: 732 · Die Stele für Kül Tegin wird fertig

summary.de: Neben Bilges alttürkischer Ansprache steht die chinesische Würdigung des Tang-Kaisers. Yollug Tegin vermerkt zwanzig Tage Arbeit an Stein und Wand.
summary.en: Bilge’s address in Old Turkic shares the stone with the Tang emperor’s Chinese tribute. Yollug Tegin records twenty days of work on stone and wall.

labels.de: 1071 · Ein Kaiser fällt in die Hand des Sultans
labels.en: 1071 · The sultan takes an emperor captive

summary.de: Bei Mantzikert gerät Romanos IV. in die Gewalt Alp Arslans. Der Sultan lässt ihn frei. Der Punkt markiert die historisch belegte Stadt als Orientierung für das Geschehen in ihrer Umgebung.
summary.en: Romanos IV fell into Alp Arslan’s hands near Manzikert and was released. The location of the historic town serves as a reference point for the encounter in its vicinity.

labels.de: 1072 bis etwa 1074/77 · Was ein Leser in Bagdad mit dem Mond anfangen konnte
labels.en: 1072 to c. 1074/77 · What the moon could teach a reader in Baghdad

summary.de: Unter ay erläutert Mahmud einen Vers und ein Sprichwort. Der Punkt steht für den Abbasidenhof, an den er sich wandte. Die genaue Zeit seiner letzten Überarbeitung ist umstritten.
summary.en: Mahmud explains a verse and a proverb under ay. The city marks the Abbasid court he addressed. The date of his final revision is disputed.

labels.de: 1228/29, Jahr 626 der Hidschra · Turan Melek nennt ihr Krankenhaus
labels.en: 1228–29, AH 626 · Turan Melek names her hospital

summary.de: Am Nordportal der Moschee treten zwei Herrscher auf. Am Westportal des Hospitals bezeichnet Turan Melek das Haus als Stiftung zur Heilung.
summary.en: Two rulers appear at the north portal of the mosque. At the west hospital portal Turan Melek identifies her foundation as a house of healing.

summary.de: Karatays Urkunde bestimmt Einkünfte, Löhne, Speisen und Futter für den Betrieb des Hans. Sie nennt sogar das Leder für die Schuhe der Reisenden. Der Punkt zeigt die versorgte Herberge.
summary.en: Karatay’s deed lays down sources of income, wages, meals and fodder for the inn. It even provides for the leather in travellers’ shoes. The marker locates the endowed inn.

summary.de: 1339 ließ Orhan vor der Burg eine Moschee errichten. Einnahmen aus einem Handelshof und aus dem Umland trugen seine Stiftung.
summary.en: In 1339 Orhan had a mosque built outside the citadel. A trading inn and property in the countryside helped support his foundation.

summary.de: Nach der Übergabe der Schlüssel regelt eine Urkunde Eigentum, Abgaben, Handel und Gottesdienst. Die griechische Ausfertigung trägt das Herrscherzeichen Mehmeds.
summary.en: After the keys change hands a charter regulates property, taxation, trade and worship. The Greek instrument bears Mehmed’s imperial monogram.

summary.de: Die Stiftungsbestimmungen von 1557 sehen für zwei Arme zusammen eine Kelle Suppe vor. Personal und Herbergsgäste erhielten andere Portionen.
summary.en: The foundation terms of 1557 allowed two poor people one ladle of soup between them. Employees and hostel guests had different portions.

summary.de: Acht Stationen verbinden eine zweisprachige Stele, armenische und byzantinische Chroniken, ein Wörterbuch, anatolische Stiftungen und die Küche einer osmanischen Stadt.
summary.en: Eight stops connect a bilingual stele, Armenian and Byzantine chronicles, a dictionary, Anatolian endowments and a kitchen in Ottoman Jerusalem.

sourceRefs.locator: In The Fortified Viking Age, pp. 78–80, fig. 5 and tables 1–2. Riverbank lane before 720, plots 6–8 m wide, Rhineland barrels reused in wells, sequence of individual coin finds and the predominance of Series X from about 725.

European Journal of Archaeology 18, pp. 497–523. The reassessment of the 1985–86 excavations at Sct Nicolajgade 8 uses domestic activity and building remains to propose early permanent occupation on part of the market site.

Archaeological and Anthropological Sciences 14, article 180. Site and materials, table 1 and figs. 1b, 7–8. ASR 9 Post Office site (55°19′44.7″N, 8°46′08.7″E). Early workshop c. 700–720, later workshop c. 760–790. White from bubbles in remelted gold-leaf backing glass and evidence for adding colourants on site.

Section “Segmented metal foil beads”, pp. 161 and 165 and fig. 5a–c (e.g. ASR9x113 59). Manufacture, silver foil, amber-brown and colourless outer glass, joined segments and the visible structure of broken specimens. Opening section on the continued small-scale production in the ninth century.
Nature 601, pp. 392–396, abstract and DOI 10.1038/s41586-021-04240-5. Single-year radiocarbon calibration placed the expansion of long-distance trade at Ribe around AD 790 ± 10.

Annual Report 2022, “Solar Event Sheds Light on Trade” immediately before “Farming the Desert”. The excavation team describes the AD 775 signal in a floor layer, 140 radiocarbon dates, and numerous imported beads at AD 790 ± 10. The photograph identifies segmented beads.
Kuitems et al., Nature 601, pp. 388–391, fig. 2. Three cut timbers from L’Anse aux Meadows retain bark edges. The AD 993 radiocarbon event and annual rings establish felling in AD 1021.

Antiquity 97, pp. 1233–1248. Introduction, Classification and chronology, Results, Discussion and figs. 2–3. Type 5 sample of 49, 42 certain and 2 probable reindeer identifications. About 0.5% of identifiable workshop waste was reindeer. Trade in finished items and movement of personal possessions are both possibilities. Fig. 3 credits the photographs of four groups to Mariana Muñoz-Rodriguez.
“Koordinate WGS84” gives 54.49104°N, 9.56623°E for the settlement. General orientation for the finds from different places plotted in Muñoz-Rodriguez et al., fig. 2.

Die Ausgrabungen in Haithabu 14. Discussion of the southern boundary, Struktur N7.6, with fig. 190: item 1778, a pointed split plank dated to 885 where a linear feature meets the bank revetment. The report traces the feature towards the harbour structures.
CHNT 2018, abstract and references. The results join excavated positions, ring-pattern comparisons and felling dates and identify major construction in 881 and 885.

Visitor plan, “The Jetty” and “Platform”. Successive landing stages reached deeper water. Smaller links between jetties created trading space. The guide explains which features of the reconstruction represent choices.
European Harbour Data Repository 7, ID_place 27 “Haithabu Hafen”. The published coordinates for the harbour are 54.492°N, 9.569°E. DOI 10.22032/dbt.38393.
Printed p. 107, lines 6–15, Old English. Ohthere gives five days for the passage from Sciringes heal to the port at Hæðum and identifies lands and islands to port and starboard.

Mitteilungen der DGAMN 27, pp. 25–29, esp. p. 28, figs. 1–2. Schild house erected in 1071 above nearly one metre of deposits. At Plessenstraße 83/3, separate excavation of plots with wattle fences and successive renewals at the waterfront.
Figure 2 locates Schild (no. 5) in Schleswig old town, alongside the site at Plessenstraße 83/3 (no. 1) and the medieval waterfront. A rounded point on the old town peninsula provides orientation.

labels.de: Auf dem Markt von Ribe und am Hafen von Haithabu
labels.en: On the market street at Ribe and the waterfront at Hedeby

labels.de: frühes 8. Jahrhundert, vor 720 · Parzellen an einer Gasse
labels.en: early eighth century, before 720 · Plots beside a narrow lane

summary.de: Noch vor 720 lagen am Fluss schmale Parzellen beiderseits einer Gasse. Der Punkt liegt im ausgegrabenen Marktgebiet.
summary.en: By 720 narrow plots stood on either side of a lane by the river. The point marks the excavated market area.

labels.de: etwa 760–790 · Ein Tiegel verrät die Farbe
labels.en: about 760–790 · Colour left in a crucible

summary.de: Die jüngere Perlenwerkstatt von Ribe verarbeitete gelbes, grünes und dunkles Glas. An Tiegelscherben aus der benachbarten Grabung lässt sich das Mischen von Farben vor Ort nachweisen.
summary.en: Ribe’s later bead workshop worked yellow, green and dark glass. Crucible fragments recovered in the neighbouring excavation preserve evidence for mixing colours on site.

labels.de: um 790, ± 10 Jahre · Importierte Perlen in Ribe
labels.en: around 790, ± 10 years · Imported beads at Ribe

summary.de: Segmentierte Glasperlen aus dem Nahen Osten tauchen in größerer Zahl auf. Ein Radiokarbonsignal aus dem Jahr 775 verankert die zeitliche Einordnung der Schichten.
summary.en: Segmented beads from the Middle East appear in quantity. An atmospheric radiocarbon signal from 775 anchors the dating of the stratified finds.

labels.en: ninth century · Combs of reindeer antler

summary.de: Die in Haithabu gefundenen Kämme eines frühwikingerzeitlichen Typs bestehen in der untersuchten Auswahl meist aus Rentiergeweih. Die Karte zeigt die Siedlung, in der die Stücke gefunden wurden.
summary.en: Most of the sampled combs of an early Viking Age type from Hedeby are made of reindeer antler. The map marks the settlement where they were found.

labels.de: 885 · Eine Bohle am Hafen von Haithabu

summary.de: Eine angespitzte Bohle an der südlichen Parzellengrenze ist auf 885 datiert. Der Orientierungspunkt markiert die Hafenanlagen.
summary.en: A pointed plank at the southern boundary of a plot dates to 885. The point marks the harbour installations.

labels.de: 1071 · Ein Haus in der Schleswiger Altstadt
labels.en: 1071 · A house in Schleswig old town

summary.de: 1071 wurde im heutigen Schleswiger Grabungsgebiet Schild ein Holzhaus errichtet. Unter dem Haus liegen ältere Ablagerungen menschlicher Tätigkeit. Der Kartenpunkt markiert das Grabungsviertel.
summary.en: A timber house was built in 1071 in the area of the modern Schild excavation. Older occupation deposits lay underneath. The map marks the excavation neighbourhood.

summary.de: Eine weiße Perle aus Ribe verrät das Rezept ihrer Werkstatt. Kämme aus Haithabu und eine Bohle von 885 zeigen, wie Menschen Handel trieben und ihren Hafen umbauten. Die letzte Station liegt am anderen Ufer in Schleswig.
summary.en: A white bead reveals a Ribe workshop’s choice of glass. Antler combs and a plank dated to 885 show how people traded at Hedeby and rebuilt its waterfront. The last stop lies across the Schlei at Schleswig.

sourceRefs.locator: pp. 1607–1609, three Tianluoshan contexts K3 level 7, layers 8–7 and layers 6–5; Fig. 2; supplement, Chronometric Data and Fig. S1
pp. 1608–1609, spikelet-base classification and domestic-type percentages; Figs. 3–4 and S2; supplement, Sampling and Quantification of spikelet bases
pp. 7367–7369, storage pits and Fig. 1C–D; Fig. 3 and Results, early CS-I, III and IV group
pp. 7368–7370, Results, Figs. 2 and 5, and Discussion: comparative husk phytoliths; biomolecular results on younger samples BWG and CS-V-03
p. S301, The Origin of Dry-Land Agriculture in North China: exposed pit profiles, uncertain dating material and comparison with earlier excavations
p. S301, sample CS-BWG from the 1970s excavations: 7,671–7,596 cal BP
pp. 3991–3993, Torihama, Results and Table 1: Initial Jōmon subset 11.1–8.0 ka cal BP
pp. 3992–3995, Results, Table 1 and Fig. 3B–C: aquatic biomarkers and different signals across sampled periods; Discussion: other preserved foods

labels.en: Tianluoshan · cultivation on the Lower Yangtze

summary.de: Vergleiche die Merkmale der Ährchenansätze mit dem Anteil von Reis unter den gezählten Pflanzenresten.
summary.en: Compare the spikelet-base traits with the proportion of rice among counted plant remains.

summary.de: Die Schalenreste helfen bei der Bestimmung der Pflanze. Zwei Datierungsbefunde zeigen, warum der Fundzusammenhang zählt.
summary.en: Husk remains help identify the plant. Two age estimates show why the context matters.

labels.de: Torihama · was Töpfe beim Kochen aufnehmen
labels.en: Torihama · what pots absorb during cooking

summary.de: Verkohlte Beläge und Fettspuren zeigen, welche Lebensmittel in einigen Gefäßen erhitzt wurden.
summary.en: Charred deposits and fat residues reveal foods that were heated in some vessels.

summary.de: Pflanzenreste am Jangtse, Vorratsgruben in Nordchina und Rückstände in japanischen Töpfen. Drei Fundorte zeigen, wie unterschiedlich Menschen in den Jahrtausenden nach der Kaltzeit Lebensmittel gewannen und verarbeiteten.
summary.en: Plant remains on the Yangtze, storage pits in northern China, and residues in Japanese pots. Three sites show different ways of obtaining and preparing food in the millennia after the ice age.

labels.en: New Ways of Living After the Ice Age

description.de: Vom Ende der letzten Kaltzeit bis zu frühen bäuerlichen Gemeinschaften. Die Kapitel vergleichen Wohnen, Sammeln, Anbau und Tierhaltung in verschiedenen Regionen. Mesolithikum und Jungsteinzeit bezeichnen regionale Entwicklungen mit unterschiedlichen Zeitgrenzen.
description.en: From the end of the last glacial period to early farming communities. The chapters compare dwelling, foraging, cultivation and herding across regions. The Mesolithic and Neolithic describe regional developments with different time boundaries.

sourceRefs.locator: Document CCLVIII, pp. 221–225 of the 1856 edition, March 1220. The Latin text gives the two-year term and differentiates the undertakings of the sultan and of Jacopo Tiepolo. See p. 222 for the duty, the exempt goods and the separate provisions for wrecked Venetian ships and captured foreign vessels, and pp. 223–224 for the reciprocal undertakings.

English Historical Review 95, no. 375, pp. 321–330. Pp. 321–325 and n. 1 discuss the Latin reply, Venetian registers, seals and dating. Pp. 327–329 explain the rate, exempt goods, shipwreck clauses and mutual undertakings.
Place 520998, Constantinopolis. Existing rounded point on the historic peninsula; this locates the seat of the Venetian official and does not identify a building.

Vol. 37, pp. 503–504. Portals and dated AH 626 inscription, raised courtyard masjid, raised platforms, lighting, water channels and conduit from Bağluca. Gives the earlier reading AH 667 for the repair.
Site 4017, description of the Sultan Han between Konya and Aksaray. Courtyard with a free-standing masjid, twin stairway, hammam and covered hall.
Section Sultanhan, entrance inscriptions and courtyard. Embedded site map centred at 38.248279° N, 33.546923° E for orientation at the han.
Entry Alara Hanı, text on the riverbank and Alanya–Konya road, AH 629 inscription, central passage and surrounding ranges, proposed uses of the outer and inner spaces, fountain and prayer room.
GPS coordinates of the caravanserai (36.692501° N, 31.724199° E) above the Description section. The article distinguishes the building from the nearby castle, river and waterfall.

In A mari usque ad mare, pp. 221–234. §2, pp. 222–223, on building scale, the Mongol victory and Karatay. §3, pp. 223–224, on the Alara Han inscription, regional setting and claims over Armenians and Franks.
Anatolian Studies 26, pp. 69–103, especially n. 32 on the two portals, the inscription of 638 AH, the disagreement over Karatay’s building role and the deed inscribed in 645 AH.

Karatay Hanı, paragraphs on the hall with rock-cut troughs and tethering holes, the two entrance inscriptions and the foundation’s provisions. Embedded map centres on the monument at 38.643978° N, 35.935351° E.

Belleten 12/45. Pp. 55–58 on kitchen and staff, 63–67 on income and shops, 84 on the 10.64 m scroll and its two faces. Edition of the Arabic deed and addenda pp. 90–108, Turkish translation pp. 109–128, esp. pp. 113–115, lines 145–230, on pay, equipment and beneficiaries, and p. 117, lines 293–295, on the written deed in 645 AH.
The Cambridge History of Turkey, vol. 1, chapter 3, sections on Köse Dağ in 1243 and the consequences for Seljuk government.

Catalogue headings Kitabe and Onarım Durumu on the location of the inscriptions, fire and the trustee Sirâcüddin Ahmed. Note 5 compares Konyalı’s AH 667 with Aslanapa’s and Dursun’s AH 677. Notes 2–3 identify the work on the builder’s medallion and repair inscription.
Own photograph, July 2008, original JPEG 4,142 × 2,330. The Summary identifies the small mosque in the centre of the courtyard. The Licensing section offers CC BY 3.0 Unported.

labels.en: On the road in the Sultanate of Rum

labels.de: März 1220 · Was kostete eine Ladung Getreide?
labels.en: March 1220 · What duty on a cargo of grain?

summary.de: Venedigs Statthalter antwortet auf ein Schreiben von Sultan Kaiqubad I. Getreide bleibt zollfrei. Auch für Schiffbrüchige gilt der vereinbarte Schutz.
summary.en: Venice’s governor replies to Sultan Kayqubad I. Grain is exempt from duty, and the agreement extends protection to shipwreck survivors.

summary.de: Kaiqubad I. lässt auf der Straße nach Aksaray einen Han mit offener Hoffläche, erhöhtem Gebetsraum und einer Halle für Menschen und Tiere errichten.
summary.en: Kayqubad I commissions an inn on the road to Aksaray. It has an open courtyard, an elevated prayer room and a covered hall for people and animals.

labels.de: 629 AH · 1231/32 · Was der Sultan am Fluss Alara verkünden ließ
labels.en: AH 629 · 1231/32 · What the sultan proclaimed on the Alara River

summary.de: In seiner Bauinschrift erhebt Kaiqubad I. Ansprüche auf Armenier und Franken. Hinter dem Eingang liegen ein Brunnen und ein Gebetsraum.
summary.en: Kayqubad I claims authority over Armenians and Franks in his foundation inscription. A fountain recess and a prayer room stand just inside the entrance.

labels.de: 638 AH · 1240/41 · Zwei Sultane an den Toren des Karatay Han
labels.en: AH 638 · 1240/41 · Two sultans at the gates of the Karatay Han

summary.de: Das äußere Tor nennt Kaichusrau II. und ein Datum, die Halle seinen Vater Kaiqubad I. In der Halle sind Futtertröge und Löcher zum Anbinden von Tieren erhalten.
summary.en: The outer gate names Kaykhusraw II and gives the year. The hall names his father, Kayqubad I, and still has its feeding troughs and tethering holes.

summary.de: Karatays Urkunde bestimmt Einkünfte, Löhne, Speisen und Futter für den Betrieb des Hans. Sie nennt sogar das Leder für die Schuhe der Reisenden. Der Punkt zeigt die versorgte Herberge.
summary.en: Karatay’s deed lays down sources of income, wages, meals and fodder for the inn. It even provides for the leather in travellers’ shoes. The marker locates the endowed inn.

labels.de: 1278/79 nach jüngerer Lesung · Ein zweites Datum am Sultan Han
labels.en: 1278/79, more recent reading · A second date at the Sultan Han

summary.de: Eine Zeile unter dem Türsturz erinnert an den Verwalter, der das beschädigte Tor instand setzen ließ. Die jüngere Lesung der Jahreszahl ergibt 1278/79.
summary.en: A line below the lintel records the administrator who had the damaged gate repaired. The more recent reading of its date gives 1278/79.

summary.de: Was schuldete ein Kaufmann am Zoll, wer bezahlte das Futter für sein Tier? Eine venezianische Antwort, drei steinerne Herbergen und die Lohnsätze einer Stiftungsurkunde führen von der Küste auf die anatolische Hochebene.
summary.en: What did a merchant owe in duty, and who paid for an animal’s feed? A Venetian reply, three stone inns and the wages specified by a founder lead inland from the coast to the Anatolian plateau.

sourceRefs.locator: Latin American Antiquity 28(1), pp. 127–143. For the 1519 foundation and its date see pp. 128–130. Figure 2, figure 3 and tables 1–2, pp. 129–134, locate the five grinding tools, stratigraphic contexts and thirteen grains identified as maize. Discussion of wild food and shellfish on pp. 137–139.
Sections 1.1–1.2 and figure 3. Coastal habitats, shellfish, sixth-century human remains, the Indigenous settlement at Morelos Park and instructions for Spanish port foundations.

Section 2, “Description and history”, opening discussion of the itineraries. Follow the sequence Nombre de Dios, coastal navigation, Chagres, Venta de Cruces and Panamá Viejo. The evaluation dates the village of Cruces to 1533, before the warehouse. Also the 1597 transfer and the relocation of Panamá in 1673.

Geographical data, component 1582rev-005, Archaeological Site of Panamá Viejo, 9°00′23.97″ N, 79°29′06.98″ W. General point for the site. Aceituno and Martín figure 2 locates the excavated square and neighbouring properties within it.

Anales del Museo de América XX, pp. 264–267, ports, the foundation of San Felipe de Portobelo, the fairs, merchandise and provisioning. Pp. 267–269, especially p. 268, the two itineraries, the municipal warehouse built at Cruces in 1536, 47 compartments, enslaved households, river transport and cargo craft.

Printed p. 186, archaeological sites inventory, “Venta de Cruces”, period Colonial. The WGS 84 UTM reference 17 P 644522 1009307 converts to 9.12836 N, 79.68478 W. It locates the settlement rather than the warehouse footprint.

Doctoral thesis, pp. 193–201 and figs. 15–26, survey near Nombre de Dios and ceramics of Lomita de Piedra. Section 5.1.1 on Luis de Mozambique. Conclusions 2–4, pp. 402–407, 1579 agreement, the rejected site, limited freedom, guarded coast, farm produce and the search for other fugitives.
TGN 7006459, inhabited place, coordinates 9.5790 N, 79.4710 W, and relationship to Santiago del Príncipe. The point marks the neighbouring port. The precise site of the maroon town remains uncertain.
Geographical data, component 135-001 Portobelo, 9°33′14″ N, 79°39′21″ W. Area of the harbour rather than an individual fair stall or berth.

Chapter II, pp. 11–17 in the 1857 edition: transfer at Gatún, steps, luggage, the reasons for hiring a private boat, fare, crew, hammock, poles, rising river and the butcher at Gorgona. The memoir looks back on the journey.

Caribbean workers on the Panama Canal, part 3 “Women in the Story”, p. 41. Dates Mary Seacole’s journey to Panama to 1851 and identifies her brother’s hotel. The date is not the publication date of her memoir.
GeoNames 3709287, Gatún Dam at 9.262778 N, 79.930000 W. Rounded modern reference for the former village site covered by the dam.
July 4, 1952, p. 6. Reprint of the December 6, 1911 account of the Chagres settlements. Passage on the old village of Gatun in the river flats, abandonment in 1908, and the site under Gatun Dam.

“Inversión extranjera y la construcción de la línea férrea”, passages on Manzanillo Island, the two port names, construction begun in 1850, 47.5 miles, the inauguration on 28 January 1855 and class fares. Later discussion of the French purchase of over 98% of railroad shares. DOI 10.18232/alhe.v22i2.588.
Chapter 2, “Migration to Panama in the 19th Century”, pp. 55–58. Origins of the railroad workforce and arrival of workers from China during construction.
“Panama Railroad at the Summit, 1855”, on the last rail laid 27 January and Robert Tomes’s account of buying oranges in the first year. Also “Barbacoas Bridge” and view of Front Street in Colón.
TGN 7006458, coordinates 9.3500 N, 79.9000 W, Aspinwall as alternative name, historical note on the northern terminus. City-level point on Manzanillo Island.
